title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
著爲成典沿襲既久經生學
子扶奇眩異綴爲新語爭相
效慕渾樸散亡世風漸斆
皇上應運中興上嘉黃虞脩明禮
樂屢
詔有司定著條章漸濯士習裁
正文體天下士固蹶然興矣
===
況河洛當天地之中河嵩效
靈世鍾聖哲風澤存焉兹復
沐被更新之化一時人文丕
變垂髫之童濡毫闈辭摻牘
之吏執帖就試矧兹髦士翕
然粹雅稽古者抽其玄辨義
者明其志陳禮樂者達其本
punctuated:
著爲成典，沿襲既久，經生學子扶奇眩異，綴爲新語，爭相效慕，渾樸散亡，世風漸斆。
皇上應運中興，上嘉黃虞，脩明禮樂，屢詔有司定著條章，漸濯士習，裁正文體，天下士固蹶然興矣。
況河洛當天地之中，河嵩效靈，世鍾聖哲，風澤存焉。兹復沐被更新之化，一時人文丕變。垂髫之童濡毫闈辭，摻牘之吏執帖就試，矧兹髦士，翕然粹雅！稽古者抽其玄，辨義者明其志，陳禮樂者達其本。
translation_en:
…were established as enduring precedents. After these had long been followed, students of the Classics and other scholars cultivated the eccentric and dazzled with the unusual, piecing together novel expressions and competing to imitate and admire one another. Unaffected simplicity disappeared, and the prevailing ethos gradually changed [?].
His Majesty, responding to Heaven’s appointed time, has brought about a restoration. Looking back with admiration to the Yellow Emperor and Shun, he has cultivated and clarified rites and music. He has repeatedly commanded the responsible officials to establish regulations, gradually cleanse scholars’ habits, and correct literary style. Scholars throughout the realm have indeed roused themselves with renewed vigor.
How much more so in the He–Luo region, which occupies the center of Heaven and Earth! The Yellow River and Mount Song manifest their numinous power here; their concentrated influences have produced sages and wise men through the generations, and the legacy of their influence and beneficence remains. Now, once again, this region enjoys the transforming influence of renewal, and its literary culture has undergone a great change. Children with their hair still hanging loose wet their brushes to compose examination writings [?]; clerks who handle documents take up their papers and present themselves for examination. How much more these outstanding scholars, united in refinement and elegance! Those who investigate antiquity draw out its profound meanings; those who distinguish principles make clear their purport; those who expound rites and music comprehend their foundations…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
述道德者發其微遡於是嘆
曰懿哉河洛之文乎其得圖
書之秘乎莘尹之藏偹乎姬
旦之制作乎顺顯之淵源乎
又作而嘆曰
明天子遐不作人功化之神一至
是乎諸士子由是升歌鹿鳴
===
振武鴻漸攄經濟之藴炳忠
亮之節樹震古之勲要無
聖明負哉或者猶謂一日之長遽
懸去取飾外者或淺中工詞
者或戾行竊爲諸士過計者
豈其然哉昔者九方皐索駿
于沙丘驪黄失對秦穆公怒
punctuated: 述道德者發其微。遡於是嘆曰：「懿哉，河洛之文乎！其得圖書之秘乎！莘尹之藏偹乎！姬旦之制作乎！顺顯之淵源乎！」又作而嘆曰：「明天子遐不作人，功化之神，一至是乎！」諸士子由是升歌《鹿鳴》，振武鴻漸，攄經濟之藴，炳忠亮之節，樹震古之勲，要無聖明負哉！或者猶謂：「一日之長，遽懸去取；飾外者或淺中，工詞者或戾行。」竊爲諸士過計者，豈其然哉！昔者九方皐索駿于沙丘，驪黄失對，秦穆公怒。
translation_en:
…those who expounded the Way and virtue brought out their subtleties. Su [?] thereupon exclaimed: “Splendid indeed is the literary culture of the He and Luo rivers! Does it possess the mysteries of the River Chart and the Luo Writing? The accumulated learning of the minister of Shen [Yi Yin]? The institutions established by Ji Dan [the Duke of Zhou]? The intellectual lineage of Shunxian [?]?” Again he rose and exclaimed: “How could our enlightened Son of Heaven fail to nurture worthy men? Has the wondrous efficacy of his transforming influence reached such heights?” Through this, the candidates ascend to sing ‘The Deer Call,’ rouse their martial vigor [?], and advance like wild geese. They will unfold their stored capacities for governing the realm, make their loyal and upright integrity shine, and establish achievements that eclipse antiquity. Above all, may they never fail their sagely and enlightened sovereign!

Some nevertheless say: “On the strength of a single day’s performance, decisions of rejection and acceptance are abruptly pronounced. Those who embellish their exterior may be shallow within; those skilled in composition may be perverse in conduct.” These, I venture to say, are excessive anxieties on the candidates’ behalf. Can things really be so? Once, Jiufang Gao sought a fine horse at Shaqiu. He answered incorrectly about whether it was black or yellow, and Duke Mu of Qin grew angry.

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
孫陽曰臯之所觀天機也取
諸內忘其外也旣而馬至果
天下之良而九方臯神其明
今之擇爾者抑亦因文卜行
取諸內也吾無方臯之明爾
獨非沙丘之品乎不然是擇
駿而駑矣〔天民〕與爾不同負
聖明哉吾固知諸士之不爲駑也
===
是役也左參政朱〔槩〕楊〔守禮〕
右參政陸〔銓〕查〔應兆〕左參議
李〔宗樞〕雒〔昂〕右參議左〔傑〕副
使張〔綸〕胡〔松〕王〔煒〕傅〔鑰〕僉事
袁〔士奇〕王〔昂〕孔〔天胤〕張〔晃〕都
指揮僉事胡〔永錫〕張〔藎臣〕署
punctuated:
孫陽曰：「臯之所觀，天機也；取諸內，忘其外也。」旣而馬至，果天下之良，而九方臯神其明。今之擇爾者，抑亦因文卜行，取諸內也。吾無方臯之明，爾獨非沙丘之品乎？不然，是擇駿而駑矣，〔天民〕與爾不同負聖明哉？吾固知諸士之不爲駑也。
是役也，左參政朱〔槩〕、楊〔守禮〕，右參政陸〔銓〕、查〔應兆〕，左參議李〔宗樞〕、雒〔昂〕，右參議左〔傑〕，副使張〔綸〕、胡〔松〕、王〔煒〕、傅〔鑰〕，僉事袁〔士奇〕、王〔昂〕、孔〔天胤〕、張〔晃〕，都指揮僉事胡〔永錫〕、張〔藎臣〕，署
translation_en:
…Sun Yang said: “What Gao perceives is the workings of Heaven. He grasps what is within and disregards the outward appearance.” When the horse arrived, it proved to be among the finest under Heaven, and Jiufang Gao’s discernment was deemed marvelous. Those who select you today likewise judge your conduct through your writing, seeking what lies within. Though I lack Jiufang Gao’s discernment, surely you are horses of the quality found at Shaqiu? Otherwise, in seeking fine steeds we have obtained inferior horses. Would not I, Tianmin, together with you, have failed our enlightened sovereign? Yet I am certain that you gentlemen will not prove inferior horses.

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
宗廟之事如會同端章甫願為小相焉
誠者不勉而中不思而得從容中道聖人
也
始條理者智之事也終條理者聖之事也
智譬則巧也聖譬則力也
易
知至至之可與幾也知終終之可與存義
===
也
引吉无咎孚乃利用禴
言出乎身加乎民行發乎邇見乎遠言行
君子之樞機樞機之發榮辱之主也言
行君子之所以動天地也可不慎乎
復小而辨於物
書
禹曰都帝慎乃在位帝曰俞禹曰安汝止
惟幾惟康其弼直惟動丕應徯志以昭

第壹場

四書

宗廟之事，如會同，端章甫，願為小相焉。

誠者，不勉而中，不思而得，從容中道，聖人也。

始條理者，智之事也；終條理者，聖之事也。智譬則巧也，聖譬則力也。

易

知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。

引吉，无咎，孚乃利用禴。

言出乎身，加乎民；行發乎邇，見乎遠。言行，君子之樞機；樞機之發，榮辱之主也。言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不慎乎？

復，小而辨於物。

“In matters concerning the ancestral temple, or at gatherings and assemblies of the feudal lords, I would wish, wearing the ceremonial robe and cap, to serve as a minor assistant in the rites.”

“To begin the ordered sequence is the work of wisdom; to complete the ordered sequence is the work of sagehood. Wisdom may be compared to skill, and sagehood to strength.”

Book of Changes

“Knowing where to arrive and arriving there, one can participate in discerning the incipient workings of things; knowing where to end and bringing matters to that end, one can participate in preserving righteousness.”

“Drawing forward brings good fortune and no blame. With sincerity, it is beneficial to offer the simple yue sacrifice.”

“Words issue from oneself and affect the people; conduct begins nearby and becomes manifest far away. Words and conduct are the noble man’s hinge and trigger. Their activation determines honor or disgrace. Through words and conduct, the noble man moves Heaven and Earth. Can he fail to be careful?”

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
受上帝天其申命用休
啓乃心沃朕心
五皇極皇建其有極斂時五福用敷錫厥
庶民惟時厥庶民于汝極錫汝保極
惟周公克愼厥始惟君陳克和厥中惟公
克成厥終
詩
于以盛之維筐及筥于以湘之維錡及釜
方叔元老克壯其猶方叔率止執訊獲醜
戎車嘽嘽嘽嘽焞焞如霆如雷顯允方
===
叔征伐玁狁蠻荆來威
夙夜匪解以事一人
無封靡于爾邦維王其崇之念茲戎功繼
序其皇之
春秋
秋公會衛侯于桃丘弗遇　冬十有二月
丙午齊侯衛侯鄭伯來戰于郎〔俱桓公十年〕
春正月齊人衛人鄭人盟于惡曹〔桓〕
punctuated:
受上帝，天其申命用休。
啓乃心，沃朕心。
五、皇極。皇建其有極，斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。惟時厥庶民于汝極，錫汝保極。
惟周公克愼厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。

詩
于以盛之？維筐及筥。于以湘之？維錡及釜。
方叔元老，克壯其猶。方叔率止，執訊獲醜。戎車嘽嘽，嘽嘽焞焞，如霆如雷。顯允方叔，征伐玁狁，蠻荆來威。
夙夜匪解，以事一人。
無封靡于爾邦，維王其崇之。念茲戎功，繼序其皇之。

春秋
秋，公會衛侯于桃丘，弗遇。冬，十有二月，丙午，齊侯、衛侯、鄭伯來戰于郎。〔俱桓公十年〕
春，正月，齊人、衛人、鄭人盟于惡曹。〔桓〕
translation_en:
…receive the favor of the Lord on High; Heaven will renew its mandate with blessings.

Open your heart and refresh my heart.

Fifth: the August Ultimate. The sovereign establishes the supreme standard, gathering these five blessings and distributing them widely among his common people. Then these common people will turn to your standard and enable you to preserve it.

The Duke of Zhou was able to attend carefully to the beginning; Jun Chen was able to maintain harmony in the middle; you, my lord, are able to bring it to completion at the end.

Book of Odes

In what shall we place them? In square and round baskets. In what shall we cook them? In cauldrons with legs and pots without legs.

Fang Shu, the venerable minister, was mighty in his planning. Fang Shu led them, taking prisoners for interrogation and capturing enemy multitudes. The war chariots were numerous—numerous and imposing, like thunderclaps, like rolling thunder. Illustrious and trustworthy was Fang Shu: he campaigned against the Xianyun, and the Man peoples of Jing came in submission to his might.

Early and late, never idle, they serve the One Man, the sovereign.

Do not indulge in excess in your states; the king will honor you. Mindful of this great achievement, continue it in succession and magnify it.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, the duke went to meet the Marquis of Wei at Taoqiu, but did not encounter him. In winter, in the twelfth month, on the bingwu day, the Marquis of Qi, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Zheng came to wage battle at Lang. [Both entries belong to the tenth year of Duke Huan.]

In spring, in the first month, men of Qi, Wei, and Zheng made a covenant at E'cao. [Duke Huan …]

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
公十有一年
取汶陽田〔成公二年〕
春王正月公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯
許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐楚次于陘
楚屈完來盟于師盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕公會晉侯宋
公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔襄公〕
十有一年
公會晉侯及吳子于黃池〔哀公十有三年〕
===
禮記
凡三王教世子必以禮樂樂所以脩內也
禮所以脩外也禮樂交錯於中發形於
外是故其成也懌恭敬而溫文
中正無邪禮之質也莊敬恭順禮之制也
君子之所謂孝也者國人稱願然曰幸哉
有子如此所謂孝也已
是故君子議道自已而置法以民
punctuated:
公十有一年。

取汶陽田〔成公二年〕。

春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕。

晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚〔襄公〕十有一年。

公會晉侯及吳子于黃池〔哀公十有三年〕。

禮記

凡三王教世子，必以禮樂。樂所以脩內也，禮所以脩外也。禮樂交錯於中，發形於外，是故其成也懌，恭敬而溫文。

中正無邪，禮之質也；莊敬恭順，禮之制也。

君子之所謂孝也者，國人稱願然曰：「幸哉，有子如此！」所謂孝也已。

是故君子議道自已，而置法以民。
translation_en:
…the eleventh year of Duke Huan.

They took the fields of Wenyang. 〔Second year of Duke Cheng.〕

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to the army to conclude a covenant; they concluded the covenant at Shaoling. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕

Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu. 〔Duke Xiang.〕 Eleventh year.

The duke met the Marquis of Jin and the Viscount of Wu at Huangchi. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Ai.〕

Book of Rites (Liji)

Whenever the kings of the Three Dynasties educated their heirs apparent, they invariably used ritual and music. Music cultivates the inner person; ritual cultivates outward conduct. Ritual and music interweave within and manifest themselves outwardly. Thus, when this cultivation is complete, the person is joyful, reverent, respectful, gentle, and refined.

Being centered, upright, and free of perversity is the substance of ritual; being solemn, reverent, respectful, and compliant is its form.

What the gentleman calls filial devotion is this: the people of the state express their admiration and longing, saying, “How fortunate to have a son like this!” This is what is called filial devotion.

Therefore, in considering the Way, the gentleman begins with himself [?], and in establishing laws, he takes the people as his basis.

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
高皇帝驅逐胡元即金陵以定鼎
文皇帝克靖內難即北平以建都今兩京並峙
其視周之東西都者可相方與下是若
漢唐以長安爲西京洛陽爲東京宋以
汴爲東京洛爲西京亦可以例論否與
然京師一也何成周歷年之長而漢唐
宋延祚之未永與
國家據南北之勝建萬世之基
皇上中興益隆繼述卜世之長與天無極而周
===
而漢而唐宋皆不足言矣然居安思危
者
帝王守成之道憂治世而危
明主者臣子愛君之忠諸士子涵育學校明君
臣之義達當世之務殆有日矣茲必有
治安之策可爲
今日獻者請第陳之
問道原於天而寄之於人人有存亡則道
有絕續原道統者謂堯傳之舜舜傳之
punctuated:
高皇帝驅逐胡元，即金陵以定鼎；文皇帝克靖內難，即北平以建都。今兩京並峙，其視周之東西都者，可相方與？下是，若漢唐以長安爲西京、洛陽爲東京，宋以汴爲東京、洛爲西京，亦可以例論否與？然京師一也，何成周歷年之長，而漢唐宋延祚之未永與？國家據南北之勝，建萬世之基。皇上中興，益隆繼述，卜世之長，與天無極，而周而漢而唐宋皆不足言矣。然居安思危者，帝王守成之道；憂治世而危明主者，臣子愛君之忠。諸士子涵育學校，明君臣之義，達當世之務，殆有日矣。茲必有治安之策可爲今日獻者，請第陳之。

問：道原於天，而寄之於人。人有存亡，則道有絕續。原道統者謂堯傳之舜，舜傳之
translation_en:
…Emperor Gao drove out the alien Yuan and established his seat at Jinling, founding the dynasty there; Emperor Wen succeeded in quelling internal strife and established his capital at Beiping. Now the two capitals stand together: can they be compared with Zhou’s eastern and western capitals? In later times, Han and Tang made Chang’an their western capital and Luoyang their eastern capital, while Song made Bian its eastern capital and Luo its western capital. Can these likewise be discussed as comparable cases? Yet their status as imperial capitals was the same: why did Zhou endure so long, whereas the dynastic fortunes of Han, Tang, and Song did not last as long?

Our dynasty commands the strategic advantages of both north and south and has established a foundation for ten thousand generations. His Majesty has brought about a restoration and further glorified the work of carrying on his predecessors’ achievements. The generations foretold for the dynasty stretch as boundlessly as Heaven; Zhou, Han, Tang, and Song are all scarcely worth mentioning beside it. Nevertheless, to think of danger while dwelling in security is the way emperors and kings preserve their inheritance; to feel concern in an age of good government and apprehension for an enlightened ruler is the loyalty with which ministers love their sovereign. You candidates have been nurtured in the schools, have understood the duties binding ruler and minister, and have become conversant with the affairs of the present age for quite some time. You must now have proposals for good government and lasting peace to offer for the needs of today. Please set them forth in order.

Question: The Way originates in Heaven but is entrusted to human beings. As people survive or perish, so the Way continues or is interrupted. Those who trace the succession of the Way say that Yao transmitted it to Shun, and Shun transmitted it to…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
禹禹傳之文武周公孔子孔子傳之孟
氏信矣然曾子子思皆號謂能體聖人
之道者也何以不與豈傳之未得其宗
與夫統必有承而堯之道果得統於誰
邪後之論道統者亦謂孟子既沒至周
程而後得其傳程子既沒至朱子而後
得其傳信矣然康節橫渠南軒東萊皆
同時相講論性道者也何以不及豈所
造之或異與夫學必有師而濂溪之學
===
抑果何所授邪且程子之學於濂溪猶
朱子之學於延平也論道之傳者則以
程子繼濂溪而不以朱子繼延平何邪
豈發端之功雖同而中正之極有別與
且以程氏之門言之切問近思勇於克
己窮探力索所得最深是皆所謂升堂
覩奥者也雖其師亦以吾道有望與吾
道已南許之矣不知異時衣鉢之傳亦
有受之否邪以朱氏之門言之明睿端
punctuated: 禹，禹傳之文武周公孔子，孔子傳之孟氏，信矣。然曾子、子思皆號謂能體聖人之道者也，何以不與？豈傳之未得其宗與？夫統必有承，而堯之道果得統於誰邪？後之論道統者，亦謂孟子既沒，至周程而後得其傳；程子既沒，至朱子而後得其傳，信矣。然康節、橫渠、南軒、東萊皆同時相講論性道者也，何以不及？豈所造之或異與？夫學必有師，而濂溪之學抑果何所授邪？且程子之學於濂溪，猶朱子之學於延平也。論道之傳者，則以程子繼濂溪，而不以朱子繼延平，何邪？豈發端之功雖同，而中正之極有別與？且以程氏之門言之，切問近思，勇於克己，窮探力索，所得最深，是皆所謂升堂覩奥者也。雖其師亦以「吾道有望」與「吾道已南」許之矣，不知異時衣鉢之傳亦有受之否邪？以朱氏之門言之，明睿端
translation_en:
…to Yu; Yu transmitted it to Wen, Wu, Zhou Gong, and Kongzi, and Kongzi transmitted it to Mengzi. This is indeed credible. Yet Zengzi and Zisi are both reputed to have embodied the Way of the sages. Why are they not included? Could it be that, in receiving the transmission, they failed to grasp its essential principle? A succession must have someone from whom it is inherited: from whom, then, did Yao actually inherit the succession of the Way?

Later writers on the succession of the Way likewise maintain that, after Mengzi died, only with Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers was its transmission recovered; and that, after Master Cheng died, only with Zhu Xi was its transmission recovered. This is indeed credible. Yet Kangjie (Shao Yong), Hengqu (Zhang Zai), Nanxuan (Zhang Shi), and Donglai (Lü Zuqian) were all men who discussed human nature and the Way with their respective contemporaries. Why are they not mentioned? Could their attainments have differed? Learning must have a teacher: from whom, then, did Lianxi (Zhou Dunyi) actually receive his learning?

Moreover, Master Cheng’s study under Lianxi was like Zhu Xi’s study under Yanping (Li Tong). Why do those who discuss the transmission of the Way make Master Cheng the successor to Lianxi, but do not make Zhu Xi the successor to Yanping? Could it be that, although their contributions in initiating their pupils’ learning were alike, they differed in their ultimate attainment of centrality and correctness?

Consider, moreover, the disciples of the Cheng school. They asked searching questions and reflected on matters close at hand, were courageous in overcoming the self, investigated exhaustively and searched strenuously, and attained the deepest understanding. These were all men who could be said to have ascended the hall and beheld its inner recesses. Even their teacher commended them with the words, ‘There is hope for my Way,’ and ‘My Way has now gone south.’ Yet did any of them later receive the robe and bowl of succession? As for the disciples of the Zhu school, they were perceptive, wise, and upright…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
莊造詣純篤博聞精識剖析秋毫是皆
所謂親承面領者也雖其師亦云斯道
有望與以天道之妙語之矣不知晚年
牌篛之屬果有承之否耶自是而後有
學師朱子而濂洛之道益明有慕尚邵
子而自任斯文之重論世君子亦稱其
有扶植人極之功自致聖賢之道不知
果可以與道統之傳否與夫必知傳道
之人則可以為造道之極諸生學道有
===
曰必明辨於此矣請詳言之以開吾惑
問漢之黨錮唐之藩鎮宋之新法皆一代
治亂之機其始也必有以致之其繼也
必有以激之其終也必有以成之可得
而聞其詳與夫人之不能皆賢法之不
能無弊在唐虞三代之時亦不能免釁
生而豫防勢熾而善處此治之所以不
可及耳漢唐宋一時賢人君子亦有見
於未然而深憂遠慮者有欲斡旋調停
punctuated:
莊，造詣純篤，博聞精識，剖析秋毫，是皆所謂親承面領者也。雖其師亦云「斯道有望」，與以天道之妙語之矣，不知晚年牌篛之屬，果有承之否耶？自是而後，有學師朱子而濂洛之道益明，有慕尚邵子而自任斯文之重。論世君子亦稱其有扶植人極之功，自致聖賢之道，不知果可以與道統之傳否與？夫必知傳道之人，則可以為造道之極。諸生學道有曰，必明辨於此矣。請詳言之，以開吾惑。
問：漢之黨錮、唐之藩鎮、宋之新法，皆一代治亂之機。其始也，必有以致之；其繼也，必有以激之；其終也，必有以成之。可得而聞其詳與？夫人之不能皆賢，法之不能無弊，在唐虞三代之時亦不能免。釁生而豫防，勢熾而善處，此治之所以不可及耳。漢、唐、宋一時賢人君子，亦有見於未然而深憂遠慮者，有欲斡旋調停
translation_en:
…dignified, with pure and earnest attainments, broad learning and discerning understanding, able to distinguish matters as fine as an autumn hair: these were all men said to have received instruction personally, face to face. Even their teacher said, “There is hope for this Way,” and spoke to them of the subtleties of the Way of Heaven. Yet did anyone actually inherit the “tablets and bamboo sheaths” [?] of his later years? Thereafter, some took Master Zhu as their teacher in learning and further clarified the Way of Lianxi and Luoyang; others admired Master Shao and assumed responsibility for the weighty charge of this cultural tradition. Gentlemen who assess the men of past ages likewise praised them for helping establish the highest standard of human conduct and attaining the Way of the sages and worthies through their own efforts. But can they truly be counted among those who transmitted the succession of the Way? Only by knowing the men who transmitted the Way can one reach the highest attainment in it. You students have studied the Way for some time [?], and surely can distinguish these matters clearly. Please explain them fully to dispel my doubts.
Question: The prohibitions against partisan affiliations under the Han, the regional military commands under the Tang, and the New Policies under the Song were all turning points between order and disorder in their respective dynasties. At their inception, something must have brought them about; as they developed, something must have intensified them; and in the end, something must have brought them to their culmination. May I hear the details? That people cannot all be worthy and that laws cannot be free of defects were conditions unavoidable even in the times of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties. When trouble arose, they took precautions in advance; when its force grew fierce, they handled it well. This alone accounts for the unsurpassed quality of their government. Among the worthy men and gentlemen of the Han, Tang, and Song, there were also those who foresaw events before they occurred and reflected on them with deep concern and far-reaching foresight, and those who wished to mediate and reconcile…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
而期不至於大敗者其說具載史冊然
皆不獲信用於當時至今有遺慨焉夫
天下之事何必盡同有似黨錮藩鎮新
法而勢不可彌者不可不思所以處之
則當時賢人君子之議論不可不講也
幸明言之毋略
問箕子洪範庶徵脩五事休徵應失五事
咎徵應漢儒作傳以演其說果得其意
否與後世論者乃力詆之亦何所見與
===
然泛觀傳記所載者有曰天雨粟有曰
天降秬秠有曰慶雲興有曰電光繞北
斗則五事何脩而得此也有曰震雷擊
齊臺有曰虹垂飲於宮井有曰太白食
昴有曰枉矢光熒襲於月則五事何失
而致此也尚有可議者力行恭儉海內
富庶乃有日蝕地震之災荒淫多慾幾
蹈覆亡乃有赤鴈芝房之瑞抑又何與
洪惟我
punctuated:
而期不至於大敗者，其說具載史冊，然皆不獲信用於當時，至今有遺慨焉。夫天下之事，何必盡同？有似黨錮、藩鎮、新法而勢不可彌者，不可不思所以處之，則當時賢人君子之議論不可不講也。幸明言之，毋略。

問：箕子《洪範》庶徵，脩五事，休徵應；失五事，咎徵應。漢儒作傳以演其說，果得其意否與？後世論者乃力詆之，亦何所見與？然泛觀傳記所載者，有曰天雨粟，有曰天降秬秠，有曰慶雲興，有曰電光繞北斗，則五事何脩而得此也？有曰震雷擊齊臺，有曰虹垂飲於宮井，有曰太白食昴，有曰枉矢光熒襲於月，則五事何失而致此也？尚有可議者：力行恭儉，海內富庶，乃有日蝕地震之災；荒淫多慾，幾蹈覆亡，乃有赤鴈芝房之瑞，抑又何與？洪惟我
translation_en:
…and hoped thereby to avert a great debacle. Their proposals are fully recorded in the histories, yet none won trust or acceptance in their own time, leaving grounds for regret even today. Must the affairs of the world be identical in every respect? When circumstances resemble the party proscriptions, the regional military commands, or the New Policies, and their momentum can no longer be checked, we must consider how to deal with them. We must therefore also study the arguments of the worthy and upright men of those times. Please explain these clearly, omitting nothing.

Question: In the section on the various signs in Jizi’s “Great Plan” (Hongfan), when the five activities are properly cultivated, favorable signs respond; when the five activities are mishandled, adverse signs respond. Han scholars wrote commentaries to elaborate this teaching. Did they truly grasp its meaning? Later commentators vehemently attacked it: what insight informed their position?

Yet, surveying the accounts recorded in commentaries and histories, we find reports that Heaven rained down grain, that Heaven sent down the black millets ju and pi, that auspicious clouds arose, and that lightning encircled the Northern Dipper. What cultivation of the five activities brought these about? There are reports that thunder struck the terrace of Qi, that a rainbow descended to drink from a palace well, that Venus eclipsed the Pleiades, and that the gleaming light of a “crooked arrow” meteor assailed the moon. What failure in the five activities caused these?

There is still more to discuss. When reverence and frugality were diligently practiced and all within the seas enjoyed prosperity, there nevertheless occurred the calamities of solar eclipses and earthquakes. When debauchery and excessive desires nearly brought about ruin, there nevertheless appeared such auspicious signs as red geese and numinous fungi. Why, then, was this so? Reverently considering our…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
皇上聰明聖智格於皇天登極以來黃河清甘
露降白鵲白鹿瑞麥瑞粟產於海宇者
恒相繼焉文明之祥中和之致無以加
矣乃今歲竊陰苦雨動連晦朔齊魯梁
宋荊楚吳越之間漂毀園廬湮沒禾稼
昏墊之嘆殆復興矣何崇盛之時而有
此邪又何災祥之並至邪招致之由消
彌之術達天人者爲我言之
問識時務者在俊傑所謂時務利與害而
===
已諸士亦知中州之利害否乎中州西
北有礦洞之利東南有黃河之害天地
自然之利固民之所利也然禁之太嚴
則有盜竊之虞取之以公不免賠擾之
患黃河本中州一二州縣之害而河夫
之累遍及一省河夫本力役之征而計
畝科產甚於賦稅其故何與夫天下之
事患不知其利害之所在故無以施其
興之除之之法今利之所出害反隨之
punctuated:
皇上聰明聖智，格於皇天。登極以來，黃河清，甘露降，白鵲、白鹿、瑞麥、瑞粟產於海宇者，恒相繼焉。文明之祥，中和之致，無以加矣。乃今歲竊陰苦雨，動連晦朔，齊魯、梁宋、荊楚、吳越之間，漂毀園廬，湮沒禾稼，昏墊之嘆殆復興矣。何崇盛之時而有此邪？又何災祥之並至邪？招致之由，消彌之術，達天人者爲我言之。

問：識時務者在俊傑，所謂時務，利與害而已。諸士亦知中州之利害否乎？中州西北有礦洞之利，東南有黃河之害。天地自然之利，固民之所利也。然禁之太嚴，則有盜竊之虞；取之以公，不免賠擾之患。黃河本中州一二州縣之害，而河夫之累遍及一省。河夫本力役之征，而計畝科產，甚於賦稅，其故何與？夫天下之事，患不知其利害之所在，故無以施其興之除之之法。今利之所出，害反隨之
translation_en:
…His Majesty’s perceptiveness and sagely wisdom reach August Heaven. Since his accession, the Yellow River has run clear and sweet dew has descended; white magpies, white deer, auspicious wheat, and auspicious millet have appeared throughout the realm in constant succession. No auspicious signs of cultural brilliance, no manifestations of equilibrium and harmony, could surpass these. Yet this year, persistent gloom [?] and relentless rain have repeatedly lasted from one month into the next. Across Qi and Lu, Liang and Song, Jing and Chu, and Wu and Yue, gardens and dwellings have been swept away and destroyed, and crops submerged. The lamentations of people overwhelmed by floodwaters seem about to arise once more. Why should such things occur in an age of flourishing prosperity? And why should calamities and auspicious signs arrive together? Those who comprehend Heaven and humanity should explain to me what brings these about and how the calamities may be dispelled.

Question: Those who understand the affairs of their time are men of outstanding talent. What we call the affairs of the time are simply matters of benefit and harm. Do you gentlemen also know the benefits and harms affecting Zhongzhou? In its northwest, Zhongzhou has the benefits of mines; in its southeast, it suffers the harm caused by the Yellow River. The natural resources of Heaven and Earth certainly benefit the people. Yet if prohibitions are too strict, there is a danger of illicit extraction; if resources are extracted under public authority, the trouble of making good losses and harassing the people is unavoidable. The Yellow River originally harmed only one or two subprefectures or counties in Zhongzhou, yet the burden of providing river laborers extends throughout the province. River labor was originally a levy of physical service, yet assessments calculated by acreage and imposed on property are more onerous than ordinary taxation. Why is this? In the affairs of the world, the difficulty lies in not knowing where benefit and harm reside, and thus being unable to implement methods for promoting the former and eliminating the latter. Now, wherever benefit arises, harm follows instead…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
而以獷犯法破家者獨甲於無礦之地
知河之害矣不惟不能除之又從而推
廣之以及于河所不害之民謂非所以
興之除之有未善可乎諸士生於中州
見上之人區畫失宜固有欲言而沮於
出位之思者姑試陳之苟可以經濟一
方他日推之天下亦可占也
punctuated: 而以獷犯法、破家者，獨甲於無礦之地。知河之害矣，不惟不能除之，又從而推廣之，以及于河所不害之民，謂非所以興之除之有未善可乎？諸士生於中州，見上之人區畫失宜，固有欲言而沮於出位之思者，姑試陳之。苟可以經濟一方，他日推之天下，亦可占也。
translation_en: …yet those who break the law through lawlessness [?] and ruin their households are more numerous here than in places without mines. The harm caused by the Yellow River is recognized, yet those responsible not only fail to eliminate it but further extend it to people whom the river itself does not harm. Can one deny that there are shortcomings in the methods used to promote benefits and eliminate harms? You scholars were born in Zhongzhou. Seeing the ill-conceived arrangements of those in authority, some of you surely have wished to speak but have been deterred by the thought of overstepping your station. Try now to set forth your views. If they can bring sound government and relief to one region, their potential for application throughout the realm in the future can also be judged.

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
矣先王制賓禮以親邦國則有會同之事焉發
禁施政而宣傳揖讓之體固有秩然而不易彈
者矣是事也君主之相從而相之服以玄端昭
其莊也冠以章甫重其瞻也亦何人也而敢以
大相自處然志在是也而願爲小相焉在宗廟
而或列於祝史之後于以翼贊乎主君之行禮
則凡駿奔登降之節固不敢自召少裡於精禋
然因之而可與聞乎爼豆之事矣在會同而或
厠于擯介之末于以周旋乎主君之共事則凡
宣傳揖讓之體固不敢自信能昭乎事序然因
===
之而可獲聞于表著之位矣夫以赤之所志若
此即其謙遜不居之辭氣固足以徵其優爲矣
抑孔子嘗曰能以禮讓爲國乎何有以是觀之
則赤之優於爲國又可知矣然夫子不取赤而
取點者何蓋禮樂之與治國皆迹也由浴沂風
雩之氣象充之則大禮與天地同節大樂與天
地同和而三子者祗見其小矣故夫子不取赤
而取點也
punctuated:
矣。先王制賓禮以親邦國，則有會同之事焉。發禁施政，而宣傳揖讓之體，固有秩然而不易彈者矣。是事也，君主之相從，而相之，服以玄端，昭其莊也；冠以章甫，重其瞻也。亦何人也，而敢以大相自處？然志在是也，而願爲小相焉。在宗廟，而或列於祝史之後，于以翼贊乎主君之行禮，則凡駿奔登降之節，固不敢自召少裡於精禋，然因之而可與聞乎爼豆之事矣。在會同，而或厠于擯介之末，于以周旋乎主君之共事，則凡宣傳揖讓之體，固不敢自信能昭乎事序，然因之而可獲聞于表著之位矣。
夫以赤之所志若此，即其謙遜不居之辭氣，固足以徵其優爲矣。抑孔子嘗曰：「能以禮讓爲國乎，何有？」以是觀之，則赤之優於爲國，又可知矣。然夫子不取赤而取點者，何？蓋禮樂之與治國，皆迹也。由浴沂風雩之氣象充之，則大禮與天地同節，大樂與天地同和，而三子者祗見其小矣。故夫子不取赤而取點也。
translation_en:
… The former kings established the rites for receiving guests to foster amity among the states; hence there were gatherings and assemblies of the feudal lords. Prohibitions were proclaimed and policies put into effect, while the forms governing the transmission of announcements, bows, and gestures of deference had a settled order that was not readily altered [?]. These occasions brought rulers together, with ritual assistants attending them. Wearing the dark ceremonial robe displayed the assistant’s solemnity; wearing the zhangfu cap lent dignity to his appearance. Who was he, after all, to dare claim the position of chief ritual assistant? Yet his aspirations lay here, and he wished to serve as a minor assistant. In the ancestral temple, he might take his place behind the invocators and scribes, assisting his lord in performing the rites. In all the prescribed movements—hastening forward, ascending, and descending—he certainly would not presume to claim even a little competence in the solemn sacrifices [?]; yet through this service he could learn about the rites involving sacrificial stands and vessels. At gatherings and assemblies, he might stand at the end of the ranks of ushers and attendants, helping his lord conduct affairs with other rulers. In all the forms governing announcements, bows, and gestures of deference, he certainly would not confidently claim that he could make the ceremonial sequence clear; yet through this service he could gain instruction at the designated ceremonial stations.
Such were the aspirations of Chi 赤. The very tone of his modest and unassuming words suffices to demonstrate that he could perform these duties with ease. Moreover, Kongzi 孔子 once said: “If one can govern a state through ritual and deference, what difficulty is there?” Viewed in this light, Chi’s ample capacity to govern a state is also evident. Yet why did the Master endorse Dian 點 rather than Chi? It is because rites, music, and governing a state are all outward manifestations. If one fully extends the spirit expressed in bathing in the Yi River and taking the breeze at the Rain Altar, then the highest rites share the measured order of Heaven and Earth, and the highest music shares their harmony. Beside this, the other three disciples appear limited in scope. Thus the Master endorsed Dian rather than Chi.

“One who is sincere hits the mark without exertion, apprehends without deliberation, and effortlessly accords with the Way: such a person is a sage.”

Yang Zuanlong

Comment by Examiner Mo, Instructor: 〔The author does not make careless assertions concerning human nature and Heaven’s mandate; this itself shows discernment.〕
Comment by Examiner Song, Professor: 〔Concise wording, ample meaning.〕

The Doctrine of the Mean identifies the spontaneous Way of utmost sincerity and attributes it to the sage. For sagehood is simply sincerity. Thus, none but a sage can participate in the original, inherent condition of Heaven’s Way.

Zisi quotes the Master’s instruction to Duke Ai on the way to make oneself sincere. At this point, he means that sincerity, originating in Heaven, is simply one. Yet once we speak of the human, we also speak of the heavenly; and once we call something heavenly, we cannot but distinguish it from the human. In what sense is sincerity Heaven’s Way? Seeking through exerting one’s strength is called effort. When sincerity issues from one’s nature, every action hits the mark: what need is there for effort? Seeking through deliberate attention is called deliberation. When sincerity flows freely from one’s nature, the mind apprehends everything: what need is there for deliberation? That one’s actions hit the mark is indeed sincerity, and it is also the Way. Since the Way does not depend upon effort, one acts effortlessly and accords with the Way. Is this not being spontaneously free from either excess or deficiency? That the mind apprehends is indeed sincerity, and it is also the Way. title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
不偏不倚者乎由誠而觀行主乎中知主乎得
也由道而觀行之中固中知之得亦中也知中
乎道是爲生知行中乎道是爲安行生知安行
非聖人而能若是乎蓋自其誠不失乎本原而
言之故謂之天其實天已屬之人矣自其人之
不能不思勉而較之故別名之曰聖其實人之
合乎天者也中庸既以誠者爲天之道又以天
之道爲聖人其旨微矣大抵天下無不誠之道
而不能無非道之誠故中庸言誠者之不思不
===
勉而又歸諸中道以誠之至耳若誠之者所擇
之善謂之實理則可謂之道猶不能無少異焉
蓋必如舜之擇其兩端用中於民然後可謂中
道此又聖人之所以終異於賢人也
始條理者智之事也終條理者聖之事也
智譬則巧也聖譬則力也
王西星

精微此作頗得其旨
punctuated:
不偏不倚者乎？由誠而觀，行主乎中，知主乎得也；由道而觀，行之中固中，知之得亦中也。知中乎道，是爲生知；行中乎道，是爲安行。生知安行，非聖人而能若是乎？蓋自其誠不失乎本原而言之，故謂之天，其實天已屬之人矣；自其人之不能不思勉而較之，故別名之曰聖，其實人之合乎天者也。《中庸》既以誠者爲天之道，又以天之道爲聖人，其旨微矣。大抵天下無不誠之道，而不能無非道之誠，故《中庸》言誠者之不思不勉，而又歸諸中道，以誠之至耳。若誠之者所擇之善，謂之實理則可，謂之道猶不能無少異焉。蓋必如舜之擇其兩端，用中於民，然後可謂中道，此又聖人之所以終異於賢人也。
始條理者，智之事也；終條理者，聖之事也。智譬則巧也，聖譬則力也。
王西星
同考試官教諭蔡批：「孟子此章稱孔子，意甚精微，此作頗得其旨。」
translation_en:
…neither partial nor inclined to either side? Viewed in terms of sincerity, conduct centers on hitting the mean, and understanding centers on apprehension. Viewed in terms of the Way, conduct that hits the mean certainly accords with the mean, and understanding that apprehends it also accords with the mean. Understanding that accords with the Way is called knowing from birth; conduct that accords with the Way is called acting with ease. Who but a sage could know from birth and act with ease in this manner? When we speak of sincerity as never departing from its original source, we therefore call it Heaven; in fact, Heaven already belongs to the human being. When we compare such a person with those who cannot dispense with reflection and effort, we distinguish him by the name of sage; in fact, he is a human being who accords with Heaven. The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) identifies sincerity as the Way of Heaven, and then identifies the Way of Heaven with the sage: its meaning is subtle indeed. Broadly speaking, nowhere under Heaven is there a Way without sincerity, yet there may still be sincerity that does not accord with the Way. Thus, when the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the sincere person's dispensing with reflection and effort, it also brings these back to accordance with the mean in the Way, simply because this is sincerity at its utmost. As for the good selected by one who strives to become sincere, it may be called actual principle; to call it the Way, however, still leaves some slight discrepancy. Only when one acts like Shun, examining the two extremes and applying the mean among the people, may this be called accordance with the mean in the Way. This, too, is why the sage ultimately remains distinct from the worthy.
“Beginning the ordered sequence is the work of wisdom; completing the ordered sequence is the work of sagehood. Wisdom may be compared to skill; sagehood may be compared to strength.”
Wang Xixing.
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “In this chapter, Mencius praises Confucius with an exceedingly refined and subtle meaning. This composition captures its purport quite well.”

宣衆音即智以一心而貫萬理通天下之故而
無餘矣終條理者樂之既闋擊玉以收其韻者

真而無外矣始以宣之終以收之則樂無不備

Associate Examiner Zhao, an Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is inherently difficult to develop; this essay provides a model.〕
Examiner Mo, an Instructor, comments: 〔It can serve as a model for the many scholars.〕
Examiner Song, a Professor, comments: 〔The writing, too, is lucid and fluent.〕
The great worthy sets forth the completeness of the sage’s Way, yet must further clarify its meaning. How difficult it is to describe the sage’s Way! He uses music to reveal its completeness and archery to clarify its meaning. The great worthy understands the sage profoundly; hence he praises and describes him in this manner. Mencius means that Confucius’s sagehood stands apart from that of all other sages. But what does he mean by “bringing together the great completion”?
To begin the ordered sequence is to strike the metal bell before the music begins, thereby sounding forth its tones. Is this not like Confucius’s wisdom? For wisdom comes first in advancing toward the Way. Just as the bell, with one tone, brings forth the many tones, so wisdom, with one mind, comprehends the myriad principles, penetrating all the affairs of the world without remainder. To conclude the ordered sequence is to strike the jade chime when the music has ended, thereby gathering its resonances to a close. Is this not like Confucius’s sagehood? For sagehood is the highest attainment in comprehending the Way. Just as the jade chime, with one tone, gathers the many tones to a close, so sagehood, in one person, fully embodies the myriad principles, giving embodiment to the reality of the Supreme Ultimate with nothing left outside it.
When the beginning sounds the music forth and the ending gathers it to a close, the music lacks nothing. When wisdom apprehends the Way and sagehood comprehends it, the Way is complete in every respect. Is this not what constitutes the great completion? title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
夫中的之機而智得乎適道之準也夫何異哉
聖者造其極之名也殆如射者之力焉蓋力則
有貫革之勇而聖則收盡道之功也夫何異哉
運之以巧發之以力善射者也先之以智歸之
以聖善道者也孔子聖智無不備巧力無不全
以故仕止久速各當其可而爲聖之時也彼三
子各極其一偏者烏足以擬之夫君子之學進
取貴宏識道貴精而立志貴遠也伯夷也伊尹
也柳下惠也皆古聖人也軻氏槩舉其事而尊
===
崇慨想之意溢於言外進取之宏也以古聖人
而各議其偏卒折衷於孔子識道之精也然必
合三聖而願學孔子者立志之遠也此其所以
爲軻與
易
知至至之可與幾也知終終之可與存義
也
王曍
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔知行非二事幾義只一理〕
punctuated:
夫中的之機，而智得乎適道之準也，夫何異哉？聖者，造其極之名也，殆如射者之力焉。蓋力則有貫革之勇，而聖則收盡道之功也，夫何異哉？運之以巧，發之以力，善射者也；先之以智，歸之以聖，善道者也。孔子聖智無不備，巧力無不全，以故仕止久速各當其可，而爲聖之時也。彼三子各極其一偏者，烏足以擬之？夫君子之學，進取貴宏，識道貴精，而立志貴遠也。伯夷也，伊尹也，柳下惠也，皆古聖人也。軻氏槩舉其事，而尊崇慨想之意溢於言外，進取之宏也。以古聖人而各議其偏，卒折衷於孔子，識道之精也。然必合三聖而願學孔子者，立志之遠也。此其所以爲軻與？

《易》
知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。
王曍
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔知行非二事，幾義只一理。〕
translation_en:
…the means of hitting the target, while wisdom grasps the standard for according with the Way. How do they differ? Sagehood names the attainment of the utmost; it is much like an archer’s strength. Strength provides the force to pierce leather, while sagehood achieves the full realization of the Way. How do they differ? To direct the shot with skill and release it with strength makes a good archer; to begin with wisdom and culminate in sagehood makes one accomplished in the Way. Confucius possessed sagehood and wisdom in full, lacking neither skill nor strength. Thus, whether he took office or withdrew, remained long or departed quickly, his conduct always suited the circumstances: he was the sage of timeliness. How could those three masters, each supreme in only one respect, compare with him?

In the gentleman’s learning, breadth is prized in striving forward, precision in understanding the Way, and far-reaching ambition in setting one’s purpose. Bo Yi, Yi Yin, and Liu Xiahui were all sages of antiquity. Ke [Mencius] broadly recounted their deeds, and his reverence and ardent admiration overflowed beyond his words: this shows the breadth of his striving. Though they were ancient sages, he discussed the partiality of each and ultimately took Confucius as the standard: this shows the precision of his understanding of the Way. Yet he brought the three sages together and chose to learn from Confucius: this shows how far-reaching his purpose was. Is this not what made Ke who he was?

Book of Changes

Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔“Only when the meanings of the words are clear can one apprehend principle without error. This〕 essay achieves that.”
Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: 〔“Concise and worthy of acceptance.”〕
Examiner Song, Professor, comments: 〔“Its understanding is genuine and penetrating.”〕
The gentleman fully applies himself to knowing and acting, and thus apprehends the principle proper to each. For incipient tendencies are apprehended through knowledge, while rightness is preserved through action: their principle is inherently so. In the gentleman’s work of advancing and cultivating himself, can either be neglected? In explaining the meaning of the third yang line of Qian, the Commentary on the Words of the Text says, in essence: when the gentleman advances in virtue and cultivates his undertakings, he must establish their foundation and must not attend to only one side of the work. Thus, the point at which principle is supremely fitting and unchanging is called “the utmost.” If one’s perception is not yet true, how can one identify the utmost in principle? If one knows it but does not reach it, how can principle be attained? Only by knowing it as what one’s own mind ought to reach, and reaching it with one’s mind, does one remain ever apprehensive of abandoning the effort halfway. At this stage, beginnings show themselves yet remain hidden, and movements are subtle yet discernible. Although the dividing point at which a discrepancy of a hair’s breadth leads to a divergence of a thousand li lies concealed where no trace appears, the stillness and concentration of one’s discernment suffice to distinguish it early and analyze it beforehand. For principle has no incipient tendency outside this utmost point. When knowledge reaches it and becomes refined, incipient tendencies assuredly cannot perplex one. When these tendencies are distinguished, virtue advances.
Principle that has already been attained and ought to be maintained is called “the end.” If one’s knowledge shifts even slightly, the mind will suddenly doubt what it has just believed. If one reaches the utmost but does not carry it through to the end, one will inevitably lose what one has gained as soon as one gains it. 也，以事處事，因物付物，無適無莫之際，雖紛然靡定，而權度之精切，可以爲質而與比矣。蓋理得而心有所制，時出而施無不宜，義固由此而存也。義存而業居矣。是則知而欲至，知即行也；終尚欲知，行即知也。義在終先爲幾，幾在至後爲義，其理一而已矣。雖然，此龍德也。使當飛見之時，不過擧此措之耳。惟其所處方危，故不免于惕厲。苟得其情，則伊尹畎畆之樂、范仲淹江湖之憂，易地皆然矣。
言出乎身，加乎民；行發乎邇，見乎遠。言行，君子之樞機。樞機之發，榮辱之主也。言行，君子之所以動天地也，可不愼乎？
黄正色
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔中字是好的感應，咸是不〕〔好的感應，結以理心二字別之，致愼言行方有下手處。〕
同考試官教諭趙　批〔天人一理，感應相同，苟能〕〔致愼，大人俱不違矣。是篇能知此意者。〕
考試官教諭莫　批〔謹愼處不苟。〕
translation_en:
… one handles affairs according to their circumstances and responds to things according to their nature. Amid circumstances calling for neither predetermined acceptance nor predetermined rejection, although things are bewilderingly unsettled, the precise application of standards can provide a basis for judgment and alignment with what is right. Once principle is grasped, the mind has a governing standard; when one comes forth at the proper time, everything one puts into practice is fitting. Righteousness is thereby preserved. With righteousness preserved, one’s achievements are securely established. Thus, when one knows and wishes to attain, knowing itself is acting; when one brings matters to completion yet still seeks to know, acting itself is knowing. Righteousness, before completion, constitutes the incipient signs; the incipient signs, after attainment, constitute righteousness. Their principle is one and the same. Nevertheless, this is the virtue of the dragon. Were the time to come for it to fly or appear, one would merely put this into practice. It is only because one’s present position is precarious that vigilance and caution are unavoidable. If one grasps the true circumstances, then Yi Yin’s joy among the fields and Fan Zhongyan’s anxiety amid the rivers and lakes would each have been the same had they exchanged places.
“Words issue from oneself and reach the people; conduct begins nearby and becomes manifest far away. Words and conduct are the gentleman’s pivot and trigger. Their activation determines honor or disgrace. Words and conduct are the means by which the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth. Can he fail to be cautious?”
Huang Zhengse
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The character zhong [?] represents a favorable sympathetic response; Xian represents an unfavorable sympathetic response. By concluding with the two words ‘principle’ and ‘mind’ to distinguish them, the essay gives one a starting point for exercising caution in speech and conduct.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Heaven and humanity share a single principle, and their sympathetic responses are alike. If one can exercise the utmost caution, the great man and they will be mutually in accord. This essay shows an understanding of this meaning.”
Comment by Examiner Mo, Instructor: “The treatment of caution is conscientious.”

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授宋　批〔說出聖人警省意甚明〕
言行極感應之大而慎不可已焉夫人易其言
行不知感應故耳知感應之大敢不慎歟大傳
釋中孚爻義若曰感應之理其端甚微而其究
甚大夫亦觀諸言行而已且言自身出耳然吾
言之必有從而聞之者聞即加乎民矣行自邇
發耳然吾行之必有從而見之者見即見乎遠
矣言行其君子之樞機乎樞運而戶之闔闢以
之機運而矢之中否以之一言行之召乎榮辱
===
也所應在人所召在我是應者非主而召者爲
主矣在人非主而在我爲主矣不待此耳言行
之發脩省而祥生聊悔而災集人榮之天地亦
從而福之人辱之天地亦從而禍之加民見遠
之道豈非徹上徹下之理乎夫言行自我若可
忽也然既應即非我之所能復與矣可不自夫
由我之時而先慎邪應感在彼若可諉也然方
感我實召之以其類矣可徒悔於彼應之際而
不戒邪大傳言此無非欲人嚴緊於言行之間
punctuated:
考試官教授宋，批〔說出聖人警省意甚明〕

言行極感應之大，而慎不可已焉。夫人易其言行，不知感應故耳。知感應之大，敢不慎歟？大傳釋中孚爻義，若曰：感應之理，其端甚微，而其究甚大，夫亦觀諸言行而已。且言自身出耳，然吾言之，必有從而聞之者，聞即加乎民矣。行自邇發耳，然吾行之，必有從而見之者，見即見乎遠矣。言行其君子之樞機乎？樞運而戶之闔闢以之，機運而矢之中否以之。一言行之召乎榮辱也，所應在人，所召在我，是應者非主，而召者爲主矣；在人非主，而在我爲主矣。不待此耳，言行之發，脩省而祥生，聊悔而災集。人榮之，天地亦從而福之；人辱之，天地亦從而禍之。加民見遠之道，豈非徹上徹下之理乎？夫言行自我，若可忽也，然既應，即非我之所能復與矣。可不自夫由我之時而先慎邪？應感在彼，若可諉也，然方感，我實召之以其類矣。可徒悔於彼應之際而不戒邪？大傳言此，無非欲人嚴緊於言行之間
translation_en:
Examiner Song, an Instructor, comments: 〔The sage’s intent to admonish and awaken vigilance is brought out very clearly.〕

Words and deeds display the fullest magnitude of stimulus and response; vigilance over them must therefore never cease. People treat their words and deeds lightly simply because they do not understand stimulus and response. If they understood its magnitude, would they dare to be careless? In explaining the meaning of a line of the hexagram Zhongfu (Inner Sincerity), the Great Commentary seems to say: the principle of stimulus and response begins in something exceedingly slight, yet its ultimate effects are exceedingly great. One need only observe this in words and deeds. Words issue only from oneself, yet when I speak, there must be others who hear; once heard, they exert an influence upon the people. Deeds originate only close at hand, yet when I act, there must be others who see; once seen, they become manifest far away. Are not words and deeds the gentleman’s hinge and trigger? When the hinge moves, the door opens or closes accordingly; when the trigger moves, whether the arrow hits depends upon it. As for words and deeds bringing honor or disgrace [?], the response lies with others, but what calls it forth lies with me. Thus what responds is not the controlling factor; what calls forth the response is. What lies with others is not the controlling factor; what lies with me is.

Nor does it stop here [?]. When words and deeds issue forth, self-cultivation and reflection bring auspicious outcomes, while heedlessness [?] brings calamities gathering around. When people honor someone, Heaven and Earth likewise bestow blessings upon him; when people disgrace him, Heaven and Earth likewise bring misfortune upon him. Is not the way in which words influence the people and deeds become manifest afar a principle that penetrates above and below alike? Words and deeds originate with me, and so might seem negligible. Yet once they have elicited a response, it is no longer within my power to intervene. Must I not exercise care beforehand, while they still depend upon me? The response to a stimulus lies with others, and so might seem something for which I can disclaim responsibility. Yet at the very moment of giving the stimulus, I myself have called forth a response of its own kind. Can I merely regret the response when it comes from others, without exercising caution? In saying this, the Great Commentary seeks only to make people strict and vigilant in their words and deeds…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
而欲慎自不能已也雖然君子固不可不知感
應之理而亦不可先存感應之心知其理則於
言行之間因應而反求於感存此心未免因感
而責備於應矣此即感之憧憧往來聖人所深
憂也理與心其辨遠矣
書
禹曰都帝慎乃在位帝曰俞禹曰安汝止
惟幾惟康其弼直惟動丕應徯志以昭受
上帝天其申命用休
張翔
===
同考試官教諭林　批〔舜禹都俞之意未易形容此作獨能寫之必通於書者〕
考試官教諭莫　批〔是篇宜如是作〕
考試官教授宋　批〔文有體裁〕
大臣致意告君以謹位而因推其所以謹也甚
矣天位當謹而謹之有道也大臣推言以告君
其責難之義至矣昔禹陳謨於帝舜之前而深
致其意先則曰都曰帝然後曰慎乃在位焉夫
punctuated:
而欲慎，自不能已也。雖然，君子固不可不知感應之理，而亦不可先存感應之心。知其理，則於言行之間因應而反求於感；存此心，未免因感而責備於應矣。此即感之憧憧往來，聖人所深憂也。理與心，其辨遠矣。
書
禹曰：「都！帝，慎乃在位。」帝曰：「俞！」禹曰：「安汝止，惟幾惟康，其弼直。惟動丕應，徯志以昭受上帝，天其申命用休。」
張翔
同考試官教諭林，批〔舜禹都俞之意未易形容，此作獨能寫之，必通於書者。〕
考試官教諭莫，批〔是篇宜如是作。〕
考試官教授宋，批〔文有體裁。〕
大臣致意告君以謹位，而因推其所以謹也。甚矣，天位當謹，而謹之有道也！大臣推言以告君，其責難之義至矣。昔禹陳謨於帝舜之前，而深致其意，先則曰「都」，曰「帝」，然後曰「慎乃在位」焉。夫
translation_en:
…and the desire to exercise caution cannot of itself cease. Nevertheless, although the gentleman must understand the principle of stimulus and response, he must not begin with a mind intent on securing a response. Understanding the principle, he examines his words and deeds, tracing the response back to the stimulus within himself. Harboring such an intention, however, he inevitably demands a fully satisfactory response to the stimulus he gives. This is precisely the restless coming and going of influence that so deeply concerned the sage. There is a great distinction between understanding the principle and harboring such an intention.
Book of Documents
Yu said: “Ah! Emperor, be circumspect in occupying your position.” The emperor said: “Yes!” Yu said: “Rest securely where you should abide; attend to incipient signs and to tranquility, and let those who assist you be upright. Whenever you act, there will be a great response; people will await your intentions. Thus you will illustriously receive the favor of the Lord on High, and Heaven will renew its mandate to you with blessings.”
Zhang Xiang
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning conveyed by Shun and Yu’s exclamations ‘Ah!’ and ‘Yes!’ is not easily expressed. This composition alone succeeds in portraying it; its author must be well versed in the Book of Documents.〕
Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: 〔This piece ought indeed to be written in this way.〕
Examiner Song, Professor, comments: 〔The composition has appropriate form and organization.〕
A great minister earnestly admonishes his ruler to exercise circumspection in occupying his position, then elaborates on how that circumspection is to be practiced. How necessary it is to be circumspect in occupying the heavenly throne, and how essential the proper way of doing so! By explaining this to his ruler, the great minister fulfills to the utmost his duty to demand difficult achievements of him. Long ago, when Yu presented his counsels before Emperor Shun, he conveyed his intentions with profound earnestness. First he said ‘Ah!’ and ‘Emperor,’ and only then said, ‘Be circumspect in occupying your position.’ Now, …

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
曰愼乃在位者蓋言天位之艱不可以或易而
忽也然必曰都以致其美曰帝以起其聽者豈
非謨謀之大而言之不容以或輕與帝也承之
遂曰俞焉蓋聞謹位之言不覺其虛受之至也
豈惟不致其咈抑且不致其吁蓋有若自已出
而先得其心之同然焉禹也因帝之俞不能自
已復繼之曰安汝止惟幾惟康其弼直焉曰惟
動丕應徯志以昭受上帝天其申命用休焉蓋
以謹位者非自位而謹之也亦曰君者謹之本
===
也苟至善之不得其止則人心惟危幾康之不
致其審則義理必悖脩之於身信乎不可以不
盡也臣者謹之輔也左右臣隣所以詔其微繩
愆糾謬所以正夫德資之於人信乎不可以或
遺也內外之脩既至則天人之理已孚由是動
而欲善而民善雖渙汗未施也然至愚而神固
有先意而徯我者聞于上帝而帝休雖無圖度
之心也然惟德是輔必有眷命而用懋者以上
則可以得天以下則可以得民是何也民之所
punctuated: 曰「愼乃在位」者，蓋言天位之艱，不可以或易而忽也。然必曰「都」以致其美，曰「帝」以起其聽者，豈非謨謀之大，而言之不容以或輕與？帝也承之，遂曰「俞」焉，蓋聞謹位之言，不覺其虛受之至也。豈惟不致其咈，抑且不致其吁，蓋有若自已出，而先得其心之同然焉。禹也因帝之俞，不能自已，復繼之曰：「安汝止，惟幾惟康，其弼直焉。」曰：「惟動丕應徯志，以昭受上帝，天其申命用休焉。」蓋以謹位者，非自位而謹之也，亦曰君者謹之本也。苟至善之不得其止，則人心惟危；幾康之不致其審，則義理必悖。脩之於身，信乎不可以不盡也。臣者謹之輔也，左右臣隣，所以詔其微；繩愆糾謬，所以正夫德。資之於人，信乎不可以或遺也。內外之脩既至，則天人之理已孚。由是動而欲善而民善，雖渙汗未施也，然至愚而神，固有先意而徯我者；聞于上帝而帝休，雖無圖度之心也，然惟德是輔，必有眷命而用懋者。以上則可以得天，以下則可以得民。是何也？民之所
translation_en:
…To say, “Be mindful of your position on the throne,” is to speak of the difficulty of occupying Heaven’s throne: one must never take it lightly or neglect it. Yet he first says “Ah!” to express his admiration, and “Emperor!” to summon his attention. Is this not because his counsel is momentous and cannot be spoken lightly? The emperor responds by saying “Yes!” On hearing the admonition to be mindful of his position, he unconsciously displays the utmost receptiveness. Not only does he voice no rejection; he does not even utter an exclamation of hesitation. It is as though the words had come from himself, already expressing what his own heart recognized as right.

Encouraged by the emperor’s assent, Yu cannot restrain himself and continues: “Rest securely where you should abide; attend to the first stirrings of affairs and to your ease; let those who assist you be upright.” He says: “In your actions, the people will respond greatly, anticipating your intentions, so that you may illustriously receive the favor of the Lord on High. Heaven will renew its mandate to you with blessings.” For being mindful of the throne does not mean attending merely to the position itself. Rather, the ruler is the foundation of such mindfulness. If he fails to find his abiding place in the highest good, the human heart remains precarious; if he fails to scrutinize the first stirrings of affairs and conditions of ease, he will inevitably violate moral principle. Truly, self-cultivation must be carried out to the fullest.

Ministers provide assistance in this mindfulness. The ministers close beside him instruct him concerning what is subtle; by correcting faults and rectifying errors, they set his virtue right. Truly, no part of the assistance available from others may be neglected. Once cultivation within and assistance without have reached their fullest extent, the principles of Heaven and humanity are in accord. Thereupon, when the ruler acts and desires goodness, the people become good. Though no command has yet issued forth, like sweat that cannot be drawn back, the people, though exceedingly simple, possess a wondrous discernment: they anticipate his intentions and await him. His virtue becomes known to the Lord on High, who bestows blessings. Though the ruler has no calculating intention, Heaven assists virtue alone and will surely favor him with its mandate and encouragement. Thus, above he can win Heaven’s favor, and below he can win the people’s allegiance. Why is this? What the people…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
助者信天之所助者順耳若然則謹位之道已
盡而治功可保於無窮矣大禹之謨必至是而
後已其忠愛之心何如邪嘗謂有虞何如其君
臣也而其治何治也舜也咨皐未已而咨之禹
禹也孜孜未已而又慎之舜上下皇皇君朝夕
將有亂然聖人之心何如是其過求也及讀易
而見苞桑堅氷之戒而後嘆聖人必有如是之
心而後享如是之治也後世時方小康君則有
滿假之心臣則進豐亨豫大之說吁何怪其治
之不唐虞邪
===
五皇極皇建其有極斂時五福用敷錫厥
庶民惟時厥庶民于汝極錫汝保極
許遷職
同考試官教諭林　批〔題本明白作者不究其〕
〔義故覺其難是卷文不窘東至講斂福錫保處〕
〔其義尤精可以錄矣〕
考試官教諭莫　批〔有詞有理〕
考試官教授宋　批〔講說明白〕
punctuated:
助者信，天之所助者順耳。若然，則謹位之道已盡，而治功可保於無窮矣。大禹之謨必至是而後已，其忠愛之心何如邪！嘗謂有虞何如其君臣也，而其治何治也！舜也咨皐未已，而咨之禹；禹也孜孜未已，而又慎之舜。上下皇皇，君朝夕將有亂然，聖人之心何如是其過求也！及讀《易》，而見苞桑、堅氷之戒，而後嘆聖人必有如是之心，而後享如是之治也。後世時方小康，君則有滿假之心，臣則進豐亨豫大之說。吁！何怪其治之不唐虞邪！

五，皇極。皇建其有極，斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。惟時厥庶民于汝極，錫汝保極。

許遷職。

同考試官教諭林，批〔題本明白，作者不究其〕〔義，故覺其難。是卷文不窘東，至講斂福錫保處，〕〔其義尤精，可以錄矣。〕

考試官教諭莫，批〔有詞有理。〕

考試官教授宋，批〔講說明白。〕
translation_en:
…what people support is trustworthiness; what Heaven supports is compliance with its order. If so, the way of attending conscientiously to one's position has been fully realized, and the achievements of government can be preserved forever. The counsels of the Great Yu would stop only upon reaching this point. How profound was his loyal devotion! I have often reflected: what a ruler and ministers there were under Yu, and what government they achieved! Shun had not finished consulting Gao when he consulted Yu as well; Yu never ceased his diligent efforts and further urged caution upon Shun. Those above and below were anxious and vigilant, as though disorder might arise at any moment [?]. Why did the sages demand so much of themselves? Only after reading the Changes and encountering its warnings about the clump of mulberry trees and solid ice did I exclaim that the sages must first have possessed such minds before they could enjoy such good government. In later ages, as soon as a measure of peace prevailed, rulers became complacent, while ministers advanced arguments celebrating abundance, prosperity, ease, and grandeur. Alas! Why wonder that their government failed to equal that of Tang and Yu?

Fifth: the August Ultimate. The sovereign establishes his ultimate standard, gathers these five blessings, and thereby distributes them broadly among his common people. Then these common people turn to your ultimate standard and enable you to preserve it.

Xu Qianzhi.

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The topic is inherently clear, but writers fail to investigate its meaning and therefore find it difficult. This essay's writing is not constrained [?]. Where it explains the gathering of blessings and their bestowal and preservation, its interpretation is especially incisive. It merits inclusion.”

Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: “It has both expression and reasoning.”

Examiner Song, Professor, comments: “The explanation is clear.”

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
君子衍皇極之疇而推其君民相與之盛焉夫
君民相與大道之公也建極之治其盛有如此
夫昔箕子衍疇以告武王君曰疇雖有九而五
則中範雖不同而極爲大禹於五之中數而第
之以皇極者何也蓋以中正貫天下之道而人
君之身則仁義禮樂之主也必叙夫彝倫而一
兆民之趨向焉高拱有清穆之尊而朝廷之上
乃表則具瞻之地也必立之標準而爲萬姓之
法程焉如是則惟皇之極建矣夫極者福之本
也極建則福自集盛德日新而吉與之俱大業
===
富有而慶與之同以一身而聚乎百順苟或不
備諸福則非建極之全功矣君人者無私福也
福歛用敷之民群黎百姓蒙平康之治日用飲
食皆君上之餘無一人之罹乎六極苟有不被
其澤則非敷錫之大同矣夫錫福於民則是與
民以極矣惟時庶民則以今日多福之受皆惟
皇之賜也非保其極則是自棄其福矣莫不彝
倫是迪遵道遵義之惟勤惟恐不協乎善而經

永膺其福豈可或外其極乎莫不標準是式會
極歸極之不息惟恐或懼乎咎而負乎于帝之
訓焉民之保極如此則於君之錫者又有以與
乎君矣君民相與如此大道爲公之治不亦有
可見乎抑於是而見皇極之大也君建極而錫
福則以民爲一體民嚮福而保極則以君爲一
心昔禹見罪人而嘆民心之不古豈非病夫錫
福之未盡而保極之未純與夫民自爲心固爲
皇極之病然下車之泣則一體之仁見矣噫皇
極之疇禹豈特能第之而已哉

夫敷錫之恩焉。惟皇多福之敷，由建極之歛爾。永膺其福，豈可或外其極乎？莫不標準是式，會極歸極之不息，惟恐或懼乎咎而負乎于帝之訓焉。民之保極如此，則於君之錫者，又有以與乎君矣。君民相與如此，大道爲公之治，不亦有可見乎？抑於是而見皇極之大也。君建極而錫福，則以民爲一體；民嚮福而保極，則以君爲一心。昔禹見罪人而嘆民心之不古，豈非病夫錫福之未盡而保極之未純與？夫民自爲心，固爲皇極之病；然下車之泣，則一體之仁見矣。噫！皇極之疇，禹豈特能第之而已哉！

translation_en:
…that beneficence of bestowing blessings. The sovereign’s distribution of manifold blessings comes from gathering them through establishing the supreme standard. If the people are to enjoy these blessings forever, how could they ever stand outside that standard? All take this standard as their model, unceasingly assembling at and returning to it, fearing lest they incur blame [?] and fail the instruction of the Sovereign on High. When the people uphold the standard in this way, they can in turn contribute to their ruler in response to his gifts. With ruler and people thus sustaining one another, can we not discern a government in which the Great Way serves the common good? Here, moreover, we see the greatness of the August Ultimate. When the ruler establishes the standard and bestows blessings, he regards the people as one body with himself; when the people turn toward blessings and uphold the standard, they share one mind with the ruler.

Long ago, Yu saw a criminal and lamented that the people’s hearts were no longer as they had been in antiquity. Was he not distressed that blessings had not been bestowed fully and that adherence to the standard was not yet pure? For the people each to follow their own inclinations certainly undermines the August Ultimate. Yet when Yu descended from his carriage and wept, he revealed the benevolence that regards all as one body. Ah! As for the category of the August Ultimate, could Yu merely have assigned it its place in the sequence, and nothing more?

In describing the great general’s southern expedition, the poet praises his mastery of the way to campaign against distant peoples and brings out his achievement in securing their submission. The way to complete victory assuredly requires both military might and strategic planning. Yet were these alone what enabled the great general to secure the submission of distant peoples? King Xuan commanded Fang Shu to campaign southward, and the poet praised him, as though saying: For a state, nothing is weightier than employing troops; in employing troops, nothing is more essential than choosing a general. Having served successive reigns at the royal court and being senior in years to the assembled lords, he was truly the venerable elder statesman of his age. Exercising sole command beyond the capital’s gates, he devised plans that ensured complete success, deploying grand strategies from within the command tent. Resting as darkness approached, he made sure that what he considered at night could be put into practice by day. 公告成王，著《無逸》之篇；吉甫贈山甫，申甫解之說。盛世君臣朋友交相警戒，皆是道也。後世諂諛興而乏謇諤之風，傾軋成而鮮寅恭之誼，視古何如哉？噫！敝也久矣！

春秋

春，王正月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。〔俱僖公四年〕晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。〔襄公十有一年〕

盧際可
〔傳意約以成文，僅見是篇可錄〕

考試官教授宋，批〔精切〕

春秋爰善霸國之師，以其皆近王者之事也。夫不戰而成功，王師之仁也。齊桓、欒書、晉悼有焉。
translation_en:
…the Duke [of Zhou] admonished King Cheng, composing the chapter “Against Ease”; Jifu presented a poem to Shanfu, reiterating the admonition against slackness [?]. In a flourishing age, rulers and ministers, and friends, admonished and cautioned one another: all followed this Way. In later ages, flattery arose and the spirit of outspoken remonstrance was lacking; mutual scheming took hold, and the bonds of reverent respect grew rare. How does this compare with antiquity? Alas! This decline has persisted for so long!

Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao in invading Cai. Cai collapsed. They then attacked Chu and encamped at Xing. Qu Wan of Chu came to conclude a covenant with the army; they concluded the covenant at Shaoling. 〔Both entries are from the fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔The sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. 〔The eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕

〔“It conveys the meaning concisely in a finished composition [?]; this is the only essay I have seen worth selecting.”〕
Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: 〔“It grasps the sage’s intention of showing benevolence toward the people by avoiding battle.”〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals approves the armies of the hegemonic states because their actions all approached those of a true king. To achieve success without fighting is the benevolence of a king’s army. Duke Huan of Qi, Luan Shu, and Duke Dao of Jin possessed this quality.

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
所以見乎於春秋且舞干苗格因壘崇降古聖
王固以不戰而服人也孰意春秋之時乃有庶
幾於此者有如楚爲鄭患齊桓伐之鄭因伐喪
繼晉救之晉悼伐鄭而蕭魚之會講焉嘗考桓
之伐楚也師帥八國潰蔡先聲楚人於是震恐
矣孰不志於一逞乎桓則以爲戰危事也苟楚
能服義吾斯已矣由是陘亭有次文告是脩屈
完惠來盟禮斯定桓之謀審矣序其成功蓋不
戰而制勝也不然倔強如楚兵力足以遽屈哉
===
書之救鄭也遇于繞角御諸桑隧軍帥胥此獻
謀矣孰不快於一戰乎書則以爲戰觀釁也今
楚師已去吾可還矣乃能信用忠言不惑邪議
戒於遷戮下令班師書之計善矣雖云無功蓋
不勝而自武也不然申息一令成敗其能逆覩
哉若悼之伐鄭也東門觀兵伯駢行成人皆謂
鄭已莫支有不戰戰必勝矣悼則謀魏絳以息
民聽武子以敝楚子展入盟蕭魚有會推誠待
物傾懷不疑而鄭自此不復叛焉是悼之功又
punctuated: 所以見乎於春秋。且舞干苗格，因壘崇降，古聖王固以不戰而服人也。孰意春秋之時，乃有庶幾於此者？有如楚爲鄭患，齊桓伐之；鄭因伐喪繼，晉救之；晉悼伐鄭，而蕭魚之會講焉。嘗考桓之伐楚也，師帥八國，潰蔡先聲，楚人於是震恐矣。孰不志於一逞乎？桓則以爲戰危事也，苟楚能服義，吾斯已矣。由是陘亭有次，文告是脩，屈完惠來，盟禮斯定。桓之謀審矣，序其成功，蓋不戰而制勝也。不然，倔強如楚，兵力足以遽屈哉？書之救鄭也，遇于繞角，御諸桑隧，軍帥胥此獻謀矣。孰不快於一戰乎？書則以爲戰觀釁也，今楚師已去，吾可還矣。乃能信用忠言，不惑邪議，戒於遷戮，下令班師。書之計善矣，雖云無功，蓋不勝而自武也。不然，申息一令，成敗其能逆覩哉？若悼之伐鄭也，東門觀兵，伯駢行成，人皆謂鄭已莫支，有不戰，戰必勝矣。悼則謀魏絳以息民，聽武子以敝楚，子展入盟，蕭魚有會，推誠待物，傾懷不疑，而鄭自此不復叛焉。是悼之功又
translation_en:
…which is why they appear in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Moreover, when shields were brandished in a ceremonial dance, the Miao submitted; when the ramparts were used, Chong surrendered [?]. The sage kings of antiquity indeed brought others into submission without fighting. Who would have imagined that in the Spring and Autumn period there would be men who came close to this? When Chu threatened Zheng, Duke Huan of Qi attacked Chu; when Zheng was involved in an attack during mourning [?], Jin came to its rescue; and when Duke Dao of Jin attacked Zheng, peace was negotiated at the meeting at Xiaoyu.

I have examined Duke Huan’s attack on Chu. He led the armies of eight states, routing Cai as an opening demonstration of his might, whereupon the people of Chu trembled with fear. Who would not have wished to press the advantage? Yet Duke Huan reasoned: “Battle is a dangerous undertaking. If Chu can submit to righteousness, I shall stop here.” Accordingly, he encamped at Xingting and prepared formal proclamations. Qu Wan graciously came, and the rites of covenant were duly settled. Duke Huan’s deliberations were judicious indeed. To recount his achievement: he secured victory without fighting. Otherwise, could military force alone have swiftly subdued a state as defiant as Chu?

When Luan Shu rescued Zheng, he encountered the enemy at Raojiao and opposed them at Sangsui. The army commanders all offered their plans. Who would not have delighted in a battle? Yet Luan Shu reasoned: “In battle one must watch for an opening. Now that Chu’s army has departed, we may return.” He was thus able to trust and follow loyal counsel without being misled by unsound proposals. Taking warning against transferring the slaughter to others, he ordered the army home. Luan Shu’s strategy was excellent indeed. Though it was said that he achieved nothing, he displayed martial strength without winning a battle. Otherwise, had a single order sent the troops of Shen and Xi into action, could anyone have foreseen success or failure?

As for Duke Dao’s attack on Zheng, he displayed his troops at the eastern gate, and Bo Pian went to negotiate peace. Everyone said that Zheng could no longer hold out: they might refrain from fighting, but if they fought, victory was certain. Duke Dao, however, consulted Wei Jiang on giving the people respite and heeded Wuzi’s advice on wearing down Chu. Zizhan came to enter a covenant, and a meeting was held at Xiaoyu. The duke treated others with complete sincerity, opening his heart without suspicion, and from this time onward Zheng no longer rebelled. Thus Duke Dao’s achievement, too…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
成於不戰也否則反覆如鄭安能致其父從弑
是則桓也書也悼也皆以不戰而成功則固仁
人之心王者之事也春秋樂與人爲善而不沒
其功故皆特書而善其事也與雖然桓君可與
而行荒業怠無補於道書若可善而弑君幽國
不可以訓悼若可賢而通吴失陳亦未爲善也
春秋之取於齊晉其亦弗獲已也
公會晉侯及吴子于黄池〔哀公十有三年〕
朱惟一
===
同考試官教諭龔　批〔此題作者往往傳外生意過於穿鑿簡約明白僅得是篇〕
考試官教諭莫　批〔得謹嚴之旨〕
考試官教授宋　批〔能發傳意〕
觀春秋夷夏講好之書見聖人治内禦外之意
蓋夷不謀夏古之制也黄池之會所以致意於
書法與且吴本東夷憑陵中國黄池之會固其
所主也然吴主會而先晉吴稱王而書子者何
聖人之意豈不以晉之主會自文襄以來未之
punctuated:
成於不戰也。否則，反覆如鄭，安能致其父從弑？是則桓也、書也、悼也，皆以不戰而成功，則固仁人之心、王者之事也。《春秋》樂與人爲善，而不沒其功，故皆特書而善其事也與？雖然，桓君可與，而行荒業怠，無補於道；書若可善，而弑君幽國，不可以訓；悼若可賢，而通吴失陳，亦未爲善也。《春秋》之取於齊晉，其亦弗獲已也。
公會晉侯及吴子于黄池〔哀公十有三年〕。
朱惟一

考試官教諭莫，批〔得謹嚴之旨。〕

translation_en:
…was likewise achieved without battle. Otherwise, with Zheng so fickle, how could he have brought it to “its father following regicide” [?]? Thus Huan, Shu [?], and Dao all achieved success without fighting: this indeed manifested the heart of a humane man and the deeds of a true king. The Spring and Autumn Annals gladly encourages people to do good and does not efface their accomplishments. Was this not why it expressly recorded each of these affairs and approved their conduct? Nevertheless, although Lord Huan deserves approval, his dissolute conduct and neglect of his undertaking did nothing to advance the Way. Although Shu [?] seems deserving of praise, murdering his ruler and confining the state [?] cannot serve as an example. Although Dao seems worthy, his dealings with Wu and loss of Chen were likewise less than good. The approval that the Spring and Autumn Annals accorded Qi and Jin was surely a matter of having no alternative.
“The duke met with the Marquis of Jin and the Viscount of Wu at Huangchi.” 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Ai.〕
Zhu Weiyi.
