title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
有改也何晉定之弗競與吳之僭王自壽夢以
來未之及正也今夫差則益横矣爭長之辨雖
強夷伯之分尚㓨苟以其強先之則人將謂夷
狄伯中國矣惡乎可故先晉以紀常不與吳人
之得先焉兵威雖雄于天下曆數未改于東周
苟以王爵與之則人將謂吳人有常尊矣惡乎
宜故稱子以正名不與夷狄之上僭焉書法如
此者正以訓後世之君使知中國之勢常尊而
自治也嚴外夷之分常卑而爲備也至信任仁
===
賢脩明政事先王之所以治内者何如也而不
容以不講脩爾車馬固爾封疆先王之所以禦
外者何如也而不容以無事或脩禮而内親則
否泰之義所當明也不然則中國一霸外夷亦
竊霸矣何以杜其窺伺之念邪或不道而肆侮
則膺懲之訓不可緩也不然則中國一王外夷
亦僭王矣何以絶其覬覦之心邪噫此夷夏盛
衰之機所關而世道升降之會攸繫此聖人重
爲世道之憂而再以及書者若曰順天地之經
punctuated: 有改也，何晉定之弗競與？吳之僭王，自壽夢以來，未之及正也。今夫差則益横矣。爭長之辨雖強，夷伯之分尚㓨。苟以其強先之，則人將謂夷狄伯中國矣，惡乎可？故先晉以紀常，不與吳人之得先焉。兵威雖雄于天下，曆數未改于東周。苟以王爵與之，則人將謂吳人有常尊矣，惡乎宜？故稱子以正名，不與夷狄之上僭焉。書法如此者，正以訓後世之君，使知中國之勢常尊而自治也，嚴外夷之分常卑而爲備也。至信任仁賢，脩明政事，先王之所以治内者何如也，而不容以不講；脩爾車馬，固爾封疆，先王之所以禦外者何如也，而不容以無事。或脩禮而内親，則否泰之義所當明也。不然，則中國一霸，外夷亦竊霸矣，何以杜其窺伺之念邪？或不道而肆侮，則膺懲之訓不可緩也。不然，則中國一王，外夷亦僭王矣，何以絶其覬覦之心邪？噫！此夷夏盛衰之機所關，而世道升降之會攸繫。此聖人重爲世道之憂而再以及書者，若曰：「順天地之經
translation_en:
…had ever changed. Why, then, was Duke Ding of Jin so weak? Wu’s usurpation of the royal title had remained uncorrected since Shoumeng’s time. Now Fuchai had become still more overbearing. Though forceful in arguing for precedence, the distinction between barbarian and hegemon remained sharp [?]. If Wu were accorded precedence because of its strength, people would say that barbarians could exercise hegemony over the Central States. How could that be acceptable? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals places Jin first to record the enduring norm, refusing to sanction the men of Wu taking precedence. Although Wu’s military might surpassed all under Heaven, the mandate of rule had not passed from Eastern Zhou. If the royal title were granted to Wu, people would say that the men of Wu possessed an enduringly exalted status. How could that be fitting? Thus the text calls its ruler a viscount to rectify names, refusing to sanction barbarians usurping a higher rank.

This manner of recording events was precisely intended to instruct the rulers of later ages: to make them understand that the Central States’ position was always exalted and put their own governance in order, and to maintain strictly the always subordinate standing of the outer barbarians and prepare defenses. As for trusting the humane and worthy and cultivating enlightened government, what were the means by which the former kings governed within? These cannot be left unexamined. “Put your chariots and horses in order; secure your borders”: what were the means by which the former kings defended against those outside? These cannot be left unattended. If the outsiders observe ritual propriety and seek friendly relations with the Central States, the principles of obstruction and concord must be clearly understood. Otherwise, whenever the Central States produces a hegemon, the outer barbarians will also seize that title. How then could their designs on an opportunity be forestalled? If they act without principle and wantonly offer insult, the injunction to chastise them must be carried out without delay. Otherwise, whenever the Central States has a king, the outer barbarians will also usurp the royal title. How then could their covetous ambitions be extinguished?

Alas! Here lie the critical factors in the flourishing and decline of the barbarians and the Chinese, and here turn the rise and fall of the moral order. This is why the Sage, deeply concerned for that order, returned to the matter in his writing, as though saying: “Follow the constant principles of Heaven and Earth…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
皇祖之所都今之南京也鍾山龍蟠石城虎踞
非諸葛亮稱爲王者之宅乎雖六朝之君
亦嘗都之然一隅偏安江漢之餘波也豈
若
皇祖膺
天眷之全運而一統之邪幽燕我
太宗之所都今之北京也左環滄海右擁太行
非杜牧所謂王不得不可以爲王之地乎
雖以金元之君亦嘗都之然夷狄竊據日
===
月之隙光也豈若
太宗膺中國之曆數而一統之邪故槩而論之
天下財賦出于江南金陵據天下之大利
也天下戎馬壯丁冀北幽燕據萬世之大
勢也兩京不相侔乎究而言之幽燕可以
漕江南之財賦金陵不可以兼冀北之戎
馬自古北可以統南南不可以統北天下
大利大勢不皆在於北乎然以
皇祖智冠百王豈慮弗及此竊緣自淮甸而渡
punctuated:
皇祖之所都，今之南京也。鍾山龍蟠，石城虎踞，非諸葛亮稱爲王者之宅乎？雖六朝之君亦嘗都之，然一隅偏安，江漢之餘波也，豈若皇祖膺天眷之全運而一統之邪？幽燕，我太宗之所都，今之北京也。左環滄海，右擁太行，非杜牧所謂王不得不可以爲王之地乎？雖以金元之君亦嘗都之，然夷狄竊據，日月之隙光也，豈若太宗膺中國之曆數而一統之邪？

故槩而論之，天下財賦出于江南，金陵據天下之大利也；天下戎馬壯丁冀北，幽燕據萬世之大勢也。兩京不相侔乎？究而言之，幽燕可以漕江南之財賦，金陵不可以兼冀北之戎馬。自古北可以統南，南不可以統北。天下大利大勢，不皆在於北乎？然以皇祖智冠百王，豈慮弗及此？竊緣自淮甸而渡
translation_en:
The place where the Imperial Progenitor established his capital is present-day Nanjing. Zhongshan coils like a dragon, and Shicheng crouches like a tiger: did not Zhuge Liang call it a dwelling fit for a king? Although the rulers of the Six Dynasties also made their capitals there, they maintained themselves in only one corner of the realm, mere residual waves of the Yangzi and Han rivers. How could they compare with the Imperial Progenitor, who received the full dispensation of Heaven’s favor and unified the realm? Youyan, where our Taizong established his capital, is present-day Beijing. Encircled by the vast sea on its left and sheltered by the Taihang Mountains on its right, was it not what Du Mu called a land without which a king could not truly be king? Although the rulers of the Jin and Yuan also made their capitals there, these foreign peoples merely usurped possession, like sunlight or moonlight passing through a crack. How could they compare with Taizong, who received the succession ordained for the Central Realm and unified it?

Thus, broadly speaking, the empire’s wealth and tax revenues come from Jiangnan, so Jinling commands the empire’s great economic advantage; the empire’s warhorses and able-bodied men are in Jibei [?], so Youyan commands a great strategic advantage enduring for ten thousand generations. Are the two capitals not equal? Examined more closely, however, Youyan can receive Jiangnan’s wealth and tax revenues by water transport, whereas Jinling cannot also command Jibei’s warhorses. Since antiquity, the north has been able to unify the south, but the south has been unable to unify the north. Are not the empire’s great economic and strategic advantages therefore both in the north? Yet the Imperial Progenitor’s wisdom surpassed that of a hundred kings: how could he have failed to consider this? I venture to attribute it to his having crossed from the Huai region…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
江則金陵實
皇祖始都之地東南人心繫之勢不得不都南
也自北平而靖難則幽燕實
太宗始封之國西北人心屬之勢可因以都北
也伏聞
皇祖正位之後嘗有都大梁長安之議矣是未
嘗無都北之心也
太宗宮殿之成嘗有繼
皇考初志之詔矣是不過因其都北之心而廣
===
之也故建都於南者即武王之都鎬建都
於北者即成王之宅洛先後不同軌乎此
國家南北都之大畧也前此若漢高祖因劉
敬之言而西都長安光武嘘炎漢之燼而
東都洛陽唐高祖除隋亂而都長安後以
洛爲東都宋太祖受周禪而都大梁後以
洛爲西都者不過援前人之故事爲一時
之踵承漢唐以爲得策而宋則兩失之矣
豈泉歟
punctuated:
江，則金陵實皇祖始都之地，東南人心繫之，勢不得不都南也。自北平而靖難，則幽燕實太宗始封之國，西北人心屬之，勢可因以都北也。伏聞皇祖正位之後，嘗有都大梁、長安之議矣，是未嘗無都北之心也。太宗宮殿之成，嘗有繼皇考初志之詔矣，是不過因其都北之心而廣之也。

故建都於南者，即武王之都鎬；建都於北者，即成王之宅洛。先後不同軌乎？此國家南北都之大畧也。前此，若漢高祖因劉敬之言而西都長安，光武嘘炎漢之燼而東都洛陽，唐高祖除隋亂而都長安，後以洛爲東都，宋太祖受周禪而都大梁，後以洛爲西都者，不過援前人之故事，爲一時之踵承。漢、唐以爲得策，而宋則兩失之矣。豈泉歟？
translation_en:
…the Yangzi River, Jinling was indeed the place where the Imperial Ancestor first established his capital. The hearts of the people of the southeast were bound to it, and circumstances made a southern capital necessary. When Taizong set out from Beiping to “pacify the troubles,” You-Yan was indeed the territory where he had first been enfeoffed. The hearts of the people of the northwest were attached to him, and these circumstances could be used to establish a northern capital. I have respectfully heard that, after the Imperial Ancestor took the throne, there were proposals to establish the capital at Daliang or Chang’an. Thus, he had by no means lacked the intention of establishing a northern capital. When Taizong’s palaces were completed, he issued an edict about carrying forward his late imperial father’s original intention. He was therefore merely taking up and extending that intention to establish a northern capital.

Thus, establishing the capital in the south was like King Wu’s establishment of his capital at Hao; establishing it in the north was like King Cheng’s taking up residence at Luo. Did not the earlier and later actions follow the same course? Such is the broad outline of our dynasty’s southern and northern capitals. In earlier times, Gaozu of Han followed Liu Jing’s advice and established his capital in the west at Chang’an; Guangwu breathed life into the embers of the Han’s fire and established his capital in the east at Luoyang; Gaozu of Tang ended the disorder of the Sui and established his capital at Chang’an, with Luo subsequently designated the Eastern Capital; and Taizu of Song received the throne through the Zhou’s abdication and established his capital at Daliang, with Luo subsequently designated the Western Capital. These were merely instances of invoking earlier precedents and following them to meet the needs of the moment. Han and Tang thereby achieved sound policies, whereas Song failed in both choices. Could this really be so [?]?

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
國家例論𢦏〔至〕〔我〕享國之數八百年於周四
百年於漢三百年於唐於宋者要之因國
勢而兼培以仁義周之所以長也恃國勢
而徒雜以智術漢唐宋之所以短也又豈
可與
國家並論𢦏執事又謂
皇上善繼善述卜世之長與天無極者非以其
能致
中興之業邪蓋自正德以來天下日敝矣
===
皇上起而振之稟乾剛神聖之資緝熙精明博大
之治紀綱法度煥然一新正彝倫之典脩
禮樂之制敬
天肇雨郊之祀孝
先弘九廟之規
親蠶有行籍田有耕國學有
幸無逸有亭主敬有箴稽古禮文之事蔚乎盛
矣由是
至誠感格
punctuated: 國家例論𢦏〔至〕〔我〕？享國之數，八百年於周，四百年於漢，三百年於唐於宋者，要之，因國勢而兼培以仁義，周之所以長也；恃國勢而徒雜以智術，漢唐宋之所以短也。又豈可與國家並論𢦏？執事又謂皇上善繼善述，卜世之長與天無極者，非以其能致中興之業邪？蓋自正德以來，天下日敝矣。皇上起而振之，稟乾剛神聖之資，緝熙精明博大之治，紀綱法度煥然一新。正彝倫之典，脩禮樂之制，敬天肇雨郊之祀，孝先弘九廟之規。親蠶有行，籍田有耕，國學有幸，無逸有亭，主敬有箴，稽古禮文之事蔚乎盛矣。由是，至誠感格
translation_en:
…be compared with our dynasty[?]? The small annotations read “as for” and “our.” As for the duration of dynastic rule—eight hundred years for the Zhou, four hundred for the Han, and three hundred each for the Tang and Song—the essential point is this: building upon the strength of the state while also nurturing it through benevolence and righteousness explains the Zhou’s longevity; relying on the strength of the state while merely mixing in clever stratagems explains the shorter duration of the Han, Tang, and Song. How, moreover, could they be discussed on equal terms with our dynasty?

You further say that His Majesty has admirably carried on and fulfilled his predecessors’ purposes, and that the foretold duration of his dynasty is as boundless as Heaven. Is this not because he has been able to accomplish a dynastic restoration? Ever since the Zhengde reign, the realm had grown daily more debilitated. His Majesty arose and reinvigorated it. Endowed with the firmness of Heaven and with sagely powers, he carried forward an enlightened, discerning, and far-reaching government. The principles of governance, laws, and institutions were brilliantly renewed. He rectified the canons of the enduring human relationships and restored the institutions of rites and music. Revering Heaven, he inaugurated sacrifices at the two suburban altars[?]; displaying filial devotion to his ancestors, he expanded the arrangements for the nine ancestral temples. The ceremony of personally tending silkworms has been performed; the ritual field has been plowed; the Imperial University has received imperial visits; a Pavilion of No Ease has been established; and an Admonition on Maintaining Reverence has been composed. Undertakings that investigate antiquity and give form to ritual observance have flourished magnificently. Through these, his utmost sincerity moved and reached …

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
天効其靈和氣協應比者
前星大耀
三皇嗣繼生本支競茂中外交歡
九廟在天之靈殊亦慰矣功光
祖宗業垂後裔雖商之高宗周之宣王奚足儷
之然愚生方欲效擊壤之歌執事顧欲聞
賈誼治安之策意者天下之患常生於意
料之所不及而愚所謂以忽之機者或不
可以不察邪然今天下殆無可言之事執
===
事適以都會策承學姑就近京邊防畧商
其槩可乎竊觀前代都關中者去邊皆千
餘里未有若今京師百里之外即爲邊關
壤連胡穴者天造之險雖不必於過虞孤
懸之勢則亦何妨於多備愚嘗稽諸往牒
聞諸故老或謂大寧都司興營等衛昔之
扞蔽山後者今則撤入畿內矣朶顏諸夷
昔之遠居隔域者今則占據近地矣自居
庸而東黄花鎮適要害之地守備可付託
punctuated: 天効其靈，和氣協應。比者，前星大耀，三皇嗣繼生，本支競茂，中外交歡，九廟在天之靈殊亦慰矣。功光祖宗，業垂後裔，雖商之高宗、周之宣王，奚足儷之？然愚生方欲效擊壤之歌，執事顧欲聞賈誼治安之策。意者天下之患，常生於意料之所不及，而愚所謂以忽之機者，或不可以不察邪？然今天下殆無可言之事，執事適以都會策承學，姑就近京邊防畧商其槩，可乎？竊觀前代都關中者，去邊皆千餘里，未有若今京師百里之外即爲邊關，壤連胡穴者。天造之險，雖不必於過虞，孤懸之勢，則亦何妨於多備？愚嘗稽諸往牒，聞諸故老，或謂大寧都司、興營等衛，昔之扞蔽山後者，今則撤入畿內矣；朶顏諸夷，昔之遠居隔域者，今則占據近地矣。自居庸而東，黄花鎮適要害之地，守備可付託
translation_en:
…Heaven manifests its numinous power, and harmonious influences respond in concord. Recently the star of the heir apparent has shone brilliantly, and three imperial sons have been born in succession. The root and branches of the imperial line flourish together, and court and country share in rejoicing. The spirits in Heaven of the ancestors honored in the Nine Temples must also be greatly comforted. Your achievements bring glory to your ancestors, and your great undertaking will pass down to your descendants. How could even Gaozong of Shang or King Xuan of Zhou compare with you?

Yet just as this humble student wished to emulate the Song of Beating the Ground, you, sir, instead wished to hear proposals for good government and security like those of Jia Yi. Perhaps troubles in the realm commonly arise where foresight does not reach, and what I called the occasions for neglect [?] cannot be left unexamined. Yet today there is scarcely any matter in the realm to discuss. Since you have chosen the capital as the subject of a policy question for us students, may I provisionally discuss the broad outlines of frontier defense near the capital?

I observe that when earlier dynasties established their capitals in Guanzhong, they were always more than a thousand li from the frontier. Never was it as with the present capital, where beyond a hundred li one reaches frontier passes, and the territory adjoins the lairs of the northern peoples. Although its natural defenses give no cause for excessive anxiety, its exposed position surely makes additional precautions worthwhile. I have examined past records and heard the accounts of elders. Some say that the Daning Regional Military Commission and the Xingying [?] and other guards, which formerly shielded the territory beyond the mountains, have now been withdrawn within the capital region; and that the Duoyan and other non-Chinese peoples, who formerly lived far away in separate territories, now occupy nearby lands. Eastward from Juyong, Huanghua Zhen lies at a strategic point: can its defense be entrusted…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
乎角山海三關古北口諸處皆受敵之衝
樊衛不尚蹂乎畿內撫臣皆有障翰之責
而薊州之控制尤切寄任或尚輕乎況營
也雖列士伍空懸勾取至而隨以放逃剌
配遣而旋即賄免弱將羸兵無裨効守鈍
戈朽甲何恃折衝夫懦弱已久積廢已深
非大振治之不可起也以愚計之惟在
廟廊咨議請
勑在廷諸臣素負經濟大畧者委以巡邊之任
付以便宜之權按行山川之險夷默察夷
情之向背一切邊防之事悉以委之或有
興舉之大利堅於必行不嫌於更張或有
增置之衆役盡於區處無惜於小費必使
重關巨鎮屹於金湯而士材官奮於貔虎
壯千里之藩籬固北門之鎖鑰外安
陵寢內保京師萬年國勢不益重乎措置既效
外而宣大遼左沿陝三鎮所當次第舉行
者亦懸容□乎昔范仲淹請築京城於仁
punctuated:
乎？角山海三關、古北口諸處，皆受敵之衝，樊衛不尚蹂乎？畿內撫臣皆有障翰之責，而薊州之控制尤切，寄任或尚輕乎？況營也雖列，士伍空懸，勾取至而隨以放逃，剌配遣而旋即賄免。弱將羸兵，無裨効守；鈍戈朽甲，何恃折衝？夫懦弱已久，積廢已深，非大振治之，不可起也。
以愚計之，惟在廟廊咨議，請勑在廷諸臣素負經濟大畧者，委以巡邊之任，付以便宜之權。按行山川之險夷，默察夷情之向背，一切邊防之事悉以委之。或有興舉之大利，堅於必行，不嫌於更張；或有增置之衆役，盡於區處，無惜於小費。必使重關巨鎮屹於金湯，而士材官奮於貔虎，壯千里之藩籬，固北門之鎖鑰，外安陵寢，內保京師，萬年國勢不益重乎？措置既效，外而宣大、遼左、沿陝三鎮，所當次第舉行者，亦懸容□乎？昔范仲淹請築京城於仁
translation_en:
…could they be entrusted with its defense? The three passes at Jiao and Shanhai [?], Gubeikou, and other such places all stand directly in the enemy’s path. Are their defensive barriers not still being trampled [?]? The grand coordinators within the metropolitan region all bear responsibility for providing a protective bulwark; strategic command at Jizhou is especially urgent, yet perhaps the authority entrusted there remains too slight? Moreover, although military camps are arrayed, their ranks exist only on paper. Men summoned to fill the ranks arrive, only to be allowed to flee; men dispatched after tattooing and penal assignment promptly bribe their way to exemption. Feeble commanders and exhausted soldiers contribute nothing to effective defense. With blunted spears and rotten armor, what can we rely upon to repel an assault? Such weakness has persisted for a long time, and accumulated neglect runs deep. Without a vigorous effort to restore order, recovery is impossible.
In my humble judgment, the court must deliberate and request an imperial command selecting ministers at court long recognized for their broad abilities in statecraft, entrusting them with inspecting the frontier and granting them discretionary authority. They should inspect the terrain, both difficult and accessible, and quietly investigate whether the frontier peoples are inclined toward allegiance or opposition. All matters of frontier defense should be entrusted to them. If an undertaking promises great benefit, they must be resolute in carrying it out and not shrink from changing existing arrangements. If numerous additional works are required, they must make thorough provision for them and not begrudge minor expenses. They must ensure that the great passes and major garrisons stand as impregnable as walls of metal and moats of boiling water, and that soldiers and military officers [?] rise with the ferocity of mighty beasts. By strengthening the defensive barriers over a thousand li and securing the locks and keys of the northern gateway, they will safeguard the imperial mausoleums outside and protect the capital within. Would this not further strengthen the dynasty’s position for ten thousand years? Once these measures have proved effective, could their successive implementation farther afield—in Xuan-Da, Liaozuo, and the three garrisons along Shaanxi—still be delayed [?]? In former times, Fan Zhongyan requested the construction of walls around the capital under Emperor Ren…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
宗社盛之日其言若迂識者固謂其能達
機也愚也書生安敢妄附昔賢位明問下
及姑就事論事無能他及也倘得進對
大廷尚有治安之大者次第陳之
第二問
楊龍
同考試官教諭林　批〔孔孟以前其道不容說至宋諸儒便自不同予能言其淺深得失之歸而〕〔復知推重朱子可以洗近時一種異同之論矣〕
===
考試官教諭莫　批〔條答詳盡〕
考試官教授宋　批〔衣折衷〕
道無存亡而其絶續也存乎人世有先後
而其同異也存乎學士之學所以明乎其道
者也學有淺深則道有得失道有得失則
心有同異故其先後相承之間統緒相傳
之致必有與與不與之殊是固有微妙之
理而不可以臆度懸斷者然則欲論其人
之道苟非有一定之見亦安能有以得其
punctuated:
宗社盛之日，其言若迂，識者固謂其能達機也。愚也書生，安敢妄附昔賢？位明問下及，姑就事論事，無能他及也。倘得進對大廷，尚有治安之大者，次第陳之。
第二問
楊龍
同考試官教諭林，批〔孔孟以前，其道不容說；至宋諸儒，便自不同。予能言其淺深得失之歸，而〕〔復知推重朱子，可以洗近時一種異同之論矣。〕
考試官教諭莫，批〔條答詳盡。〕
考試官教授宋，批〔衣折衷。〕
道無存亡，而其絶續也存乎人；世有先後，而其同異也存乎學。士之學，所以明乎其道者也。學有淺深，則道有得失；道有得失，則心有同異。故其先後相承之間，統緒相傳之致，必有與與不與之殊。是固有微妙之理，而不可以臆度懸斷者。然則欲論其人之道，苟非有一定之見，亦安能有以得其
translation_en:
…in the flourishing days of Emperor Renzong’s reign [?]. His words seemed impractical, but discerning men certainly considered him capable of grasping the critical circumstances. An ignorant scholar such as I—how could I dare presumptuously to compare myself with a worthy of old? Since your discerning inquiry has reached down to me [?], I have merely discussed the matters at hand and cannot address anything further. If I should gain the opportunity to present my answers before the great court, I would set forth in sequence further matters of greater importance to good government and peace.
Second Policy Question
Yang Long
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Before Confucius and Mencius, the Way admits of no discussion; with the various Confucian scholars of the Song, however, matters become different. I can explain where their depth or shallowness of learning and their successes or failures ultimately lie, and〕〔also know to accord Master Zhu particular esteem: this can sweep away a certain kind of recent argument about agreement and disagreement.〕
Examiner Mo, Instructor, comments: 〔The answers to the individual points are detailed and thorough.〕
Examiner Song, Professor, comments: 〔A balanced judgment [?].〕
The Way neither comes into existence nor perishes, yet its interruption or continuation depends on people. Ages come earlier or later, yet their agreement or divergence depends on learning. A scholar’s learning is the means by which he makes the Way clear. Learning may be shallow or deep, and consequently the Way may be apprehended or missed; as the Way is apprehended or missed, minds agree or differ. Thus, in the succession of earlier and later scholars, and in the transmission of the lineage, there must be distinctions between those accorded recognition and those denied it. There are indeed subtle principles here, which cannot be judged through conjecture or unsupported assertions. Accordingly, if one wishes to discuss a person’s understanding of the Way, unless one possesses a settled judgment, how could one grasp its…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
得其異同之實歟執事以道統下詢是欲
觀尚論之志而期以斯文之未甚盛心也
愚也不足以知之姑拾所聞以復明問之
萬一焉夫所謂堯傳之舜舜傳之禹禹傳
之文武周公孔子孔子傳之軻氏此韓子
之言見於原道之篇然不妄矣然以曾子
子思傳道而乃不及者豈不以曾子聖門
難以並言思爲私淑不必悉數舉孔孟則
二賢可以例見與執事疑焉以其傳之未
===
得其宗者殆非也若夫堯之道則伏羲神
農黃帝繼天立極固其一緒之相承者也
黃勉齋以爲堯得統於天者則以黃帝以
前其學未聞執中之言至堯始發爾夫豈
無所見歟孟子既沒至周程而後得其傳
程子既沒至朱子而後得其傳此勉齋之
言見於晦庵之狀固可信矣然以康節橫
渠南軒東萊之賢而皆不與者豈不以演
皇極者偏於數作正蒙者過於苦廣漢是
punctuated:
得其異同之實歟？執事以道統下詢，是欲觀尚論之志，而期以斯文之未甚，盛心也。愚也不足以知之，姑拾所聞，以復明問之萬一焉。
夫所謂堯傳之舜，舜傳之禹，禹傳之文武周公孔子，孔子傳之軻氏，此韓子之言，見於《原道》之篇，然不妄矣。然以曾子、子思傳道而乃不及者，豈不以曾子聖門難以並言，思爲私淑，不必悉數，舉孔孟則二賢可以例見與？執事疑焉，以其傳之未得其宗者，殆非也。
若夫堯之道，則伏羲、神農、黃帝繼天立極，固其一緒之相承者也。黃勉齋以爲堯得統於天者，則以黃帝以前，其學未聞執中之言，至堯始發爾，夫豈無所見歟？孟子既沒，至周程而後得其傳；程子既沒，至朱子而後得其傳。此勉齋之言，見於《晦庵之狀》，固可信矣。然以康節、橫渠、南軒、東萊之賢而皆不與者，豈不以演《皇極》者偏於數，作《正蒙》者過於苦，廣漢是
translation_en:
…ascertain the truth of their similarities and differences? By deigning to inquire about the succession of the Way, you wish to examine my aspiration to assess the ancients and express hopes for this cultural tradition, which has not yet greatly flourished [?]. Such is your generous intention. Ignorant as I am, I lack sufficient understanding of this; nevertheless, I shall gather what I have heard to answer some small part of your discerning question.
The statement that Yao transmitted the Way to Shun, Shun to Yu, Yu to Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius, and Confucius to Ke—that is, Mengzi—is Master Han Yu’s statement in his essay Inquiry into the Way. It is indeed no idle claim. Yet Zengzi and Zisi transmitted the Way: why are they not mentioned? Is it not because Zengzi, being within the sage’s school, could hardly be named alongside him [?], while Zisi learned indirectly from the sage’s legacy, so that there was no need to enumerate everyone? By naming Confucius and Mengzi, the inclusion of these two worthies could be inferred. Your doubt that they had failed to grasp the essential purport of what they transmitted is probably mistaken.
As for Yao’s Way, Fuxi, Shennong, and Huangdi succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard; theirs was certainly a single continuing succession. Huang Mianzhai’s assertion that Yao received the succession from Heaven rests on the fact that, before Huangdi, no teaching about holding fast to the mean had been heard in their learning; only with Yao was it first articulated. Surely this view was not without insight? After Mengzi died, only with Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers was the transmission recovered; after Master Cheng died, only with Master Zhu Xi was it recovered. These words of Mianzhai appear in his Account of the Life of Hui’an and are certainly credible. Yet why were such worthies as Kangjie, Hengqu, Nanxuan, and Donglai all excluded? Was it not because the expounder of the Supreme Ultimate inclined too far toward numbers, while the author of Correcting Youthful Ignorance carried arduous effort too far? As for Guanghan, this …

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
世而學未成金華博學而約則未與執事
所謂所造之或異者信然也若夫濂溪之
學則不由師傳默契道體天之所畀而與
乎斯文者也晦庵所疑希夷种放之傳則
以張忠定公嘗從希夷其論公事有陰陽
之言有合圖意故耳六者以爲師鶴林壽
涯者何其無稽之甚與彼夫春陵再見而
發其吟風弄月之趣延平平歲而親□求
壺秋月之容程朱之遊乎周李之門其受
===
受之同固矣但默坐澄心者欲觀喜怒哀
樂未發之前而主靜則過之不若著書立圖
者則見太極動靜循環之妙而體用俱全
其以程子繼濂溪而不以朱子繼延平者
得非以此與執事所謂發端之功則同中
正之極有別者是矣至於程氏之門賢才
多矣切問近思而爲克己之學有吾道有
望之許者非上蔡乎窮探力索晚年所得
最深有吾道已南之稱者非龜山乎升堂
punctuated: 世而學未成，金華博學而約則未與。執事所謂所造之或異者，信然也。若夫濂溪之學，則不由師傳，默契道體，天之所畀而與乎斯文者也。晦庵所疑希夷、种放之傳，則以張忠定公嘗從希夷，其論公事有陰陽之言，有合圖意故耳。六者以爲師鶴林、壽涯者，何其無稽之甚與！彼夫春陵再見而發其吟風弄月之趣，延平平歲而親□求壺秋月之容，程朱之遊乎周李之門，其受受之同固矣。但默坐澄心者，欲觀喜怒哀樂未發之前，而主靜則過之，不若著書立圖者，則見太極動靜循環之妙，而體用俱全。其以程子繼濂溪，而不以朱子繼延平者，得非以此與？執事所謂發端之功則同，中正之極有別者，是矣。至於程氏之門，賢才多矣。切問近思而爲克己之學，有吾道有望之許者，非上蔡乎？窮探力索，晚年所得最深，有吾道已南之稱者，非龜山乎？升堂
translation_en:
…of his age, yet his learning was incomplete; Jinhua was broadly learned, but was not accorded mastery in drawing that learning together. Your observation that their attainments may have differed is indeed correct.

As for Lianxi’s learning, it did not come through transmission from a teacher. He silently apprehended the substance of the Way: this was Heaven’s gift, enabling him to participate in this cultural tradition. Hui’an’s suspicion of a transmission through Xiyi and Chong Fang arose merely because Lord Zhang Zhongding had once studied under Xiyi, and his discussions of public affairs contained statements about yin and yang that accorded with the meaning of the diagram. As for the claim that he took Helin and Shouya as teachers—the preceding wording is doubtful [?]—how utterly unfounded it is!

After twice meeting the master of Chunling, Cheng gave expression to his delight in chanting in the breeze and enjoying the moon. With Yanping, Zhu personally sought the bearing of an autumn moon reflected in a vessel [?; the wording here is garbled and includes an illegible character]. In Cheng’s and Zhu’s attendance at the schools of Zhou and Li, the similarity of their receiving instruction is certain [?; the transcription repeats “receiving”]. But the one who sat silently and clarified his mind sought to observe the state before pleasure, anger, sorrow, and joy arose; his emphasis on stillness went too far. He did not equal the one who wrote a treatise and established a diagram, revealing the wondrous alternation of movement and stillness in the Supreme Ultimate, with substance and function both fully present. Could this not explain why Master Cheng is regarded as succeeding Lianxi, whereas Master Zhu is not regarded as succeeding Yanping? Your statement that their contributions in opening the way were alike, but that they differed in attaining the ultimate standard of centrality and correctness, is right.

As for the Cheng school, it had many worthy and talented men. Was it not Shangcai who pursued the learning of self-mastery through searching questions and reflection on matters close at hand, earning the commendation, “There is hope for our Way”? Was it not Guishan who investigated exhaustively and searched with all his strength, attaining his deepest understanding in his later years, and of whom it was said, “Our Way has now gone south”? They had ascended the hall …

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
觀矣宜乎能傳其師之道矣然謝則才高
而鮮沉潛之實楊則氣弱而少矯勵之功
故朱子謂其皆與其師不相似異時復有
二先生衣缽無傳之言由此觀之伊洛之
道固非楊謝之所得與矣朱氏之門英才
多矣明睿端莊造詣純篤而稱爲斯道有
望者則直卿也博聞精識剖析秋毫而與
聞天道之妙者則季通也親承面領卜宜
乎能傳其師之道矣然蔡之傑然於紫陽
===
之門未若黃之深造乎敬齋之妙故董氏
謂其得紫陽之正傳而嘗特精舍之託乃
欲請其掛牌秉笏由是觀之考亭之傳得
非勉齋之獨承乎自是而後魯齋之學一
以朱子爲師而陳氏則謂濂洛之道賴以
益明歐陽氏至稱其自謹獨之功充而至
於天德王道之蘊表裏洞徹而超然於不
動而敬不言而信之域其於斯道之傳宜
君可無憾矣草廬之學尤以邵子爲慕而
punctuated:
觀矣，宜乎能傳其師之道矣。然謝則才高而鮮沉潛之實，楊則氣弱而少矯勵之功，故朱子謂其皆與其師不相似，異時復有二先生衣缽無傳之言。由此觀之，伊洛之道固非楊謝之所得與矣。
朱氏之門英才多矣。明睿端莊，造詣純篤，而稱爲斯道有望者，則直卿也；博聞精識，剖析秋毫，而與聞天道之妙者，則季通也。親承面領，卜宜乎能傳其師之道矣。然蔡之傑然於紫陽之門，未若黃之深造乎敬齋之妙，故董氏謂其得紫陽之正傳，而嘗特精舍之託，乃欲請其掛牌秉笏。由是觀之，考亭之傳，得非勉齋之獨承乎？
自是而後，魯齋之學，一以朱子爲師，而陳氏則謂濂洛之道賴以益明。歐陽氏至稱其自謹獨之功，充而至於天德王道之蘊，表裏洞徹，而超然於不動而敬、不言而信之域。其於斯道之傳，宜君可無憾矣。草廬之學，尤以邵子爲慕，而
translation_en:
…have beheld it [?]; it would seem fitting that they could transmit their teacher’s Way. Yet Xie possessed great talent but little substance in quiet, sustained study, while Yang was weak in resolve and lacked the effort of rousing and disciplining himself. Thus Master Zhu said that neither resembled his teacher; on another occasion he also remarked that the two gentlemen had left no successors to inherit their mantle. Viewed in this light, the Way of Yi and Luo was surely not something Yang and Xie had fully attained.
There were many outstanding talents among Master Zhu’s disciples. The one who was perceptive, wise, upright, and dignified, whose attainments were pure and substantial, and who was acclaimed as a source of hope for this Way, was Zhiqing. The one whose learning was broad and discernment precise, who could analyze matters down to the finest detail and was admitted to hearing the subtleties of the Way of Heaven, was Jitong. Having received their teaching personally and face to face, they should surely have been able to transmit their teacher’s Way [the character 卜 here is doubtful]. Yet although Cai stood out among the disciples of Ziyang, he did not equal Huang in deeply attaining the subtleties of the Studio of Reverent Attentiveness. Thus Master Dong said that Huang had received Ziyang’s authentic transmission. He also once entrusted him with the academy [?], wishing to invite him to hang up his name plaque and take up the ceremonial tablet. Viewed in this light, was it not Mianzhai alone who inherited the transmission of Kaoting?
Thereafter, Luzhai’s learning took Master Zhu alone as its guide, and Master Chen said that through him the Way of Lian and Luo had been further elucidated. Master Ouyang went so far as to praise him for extending his practice of watchfulness over himself when alone until it reached the profound substance of heavenly virtue and the kingly Way: inwardly and outwardly, all was thoroughly illuminated, and he rose to the realm of being reverent without moving and trustworthy without speaking. In his transmission of this Way, it would seem that there could be no cause for regret [the character 君 here is doubtful]. Caolu’s learning particularly took Master Shao as its object of admiration, and…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
虞氏則謂其日就月將自致聖賢之道揭
傒斯至稱其厤研六經疏瀹百氏著書立
言師表百世其於斯道之傳亦宜若可無
愧矣但文正之仕元則君子病其失夫出
處且或譏其近於佛老之學見於靜脩退
齋之記可考也幼清之立言則後儒疑其
喜於著述而或背夫詳說反約之功觀其
學統纂言諸作可見矣則於斯道之傳亦
未見其眞可以接濂洛而承關閩也□
===
先儒所論而愚生之所聞者不知其□
否邪執事復謂必知傳道之人乃可以爲
造道之極愚未有知敢有造道之望乎但
誦說有年亦或竊見古人之一二私嘗以
爲堯舜禹湯文武周公孔孟道之宗也周
則至精而其業未廣程則至正而微言未
析許至純也或未極其分殊吳至博也而
未極其理一若大極其精貫之上得理一
分殊之義而有富業富之美者其惟朱
punctuated:
虞氏則謂其日就月將，自致聖賢之道。揭傒斯至稱其厤研六經，疏瀹百氏，著書立言，師表百世。其於斯道之傳，亦宜若可無愧矣。但文正之仕元，則君子病其失夫出處；且或譏其近於佛老之學，見於靜脩退齋之記，可考也。幼清之立言，則後儒疑其喜於著述，而或背夫詳說反約之功，觀其學統纂言諸作可見矣。則於斯道之傳，亦未見其眞可以接濂洛而承關閩也。□先儒所論，而愚生之所聞者，不知其□否邪？
執事復謂必知傳道之人，乃可以爲造道之極。愚未有知，敢有造道之望乎？但誦說有年，亦或竊見古人之一二。私嘗以爲堯舜禹湯文武周公孔孟，道之宗也。周則至精，而其業未廣；程則至正，而微言未析；許至純也，或未極其分殊；吳至博也，而未極其理一。若大極其精貫之上，得理一分殊之義，而有富業富之美者，其惟朱
translation_en:
…Master Yu said that he advanced daily and monthly, attaining through his own efforts the Way of the sages and worthies. Jie Xisi went so far as to praise him for thoroughly investigating the Six Classics, elucidating the writings of the various masters, composing books and establishing teachings, and serving as a model for a hundred generations. In transmitting this Way, he too would seem to have had nothing to be ashamed of. Yet gentlemen faulted Wenzheng [Xu Heng] for serving the Yuan, judging that he had failed to act properly in choosing between public service and withdrawal. Some also criticized his learning as approaching Buddhism and Daoism; this can be examined in the records concerning Jingxiu and Tuizhai [?]. As for the teachings established by Youqing [Wu Cheng], later scholars suspected that his fondness for writing sometimes ran counter to the work of proceeding from extensive exposition back to essentials. This can be seen in such works as his Lineage of Learning (Xuetong) and Collected Explanations (Zuanyan). Thus, in transmitting this Way, it has not been shown that they could truly continue the traditions of Lian and Luo and inherit those of Guan and Min. [Illegible] what earlier scholars have discussed and what this unworthy student has heard—I do not know whether it is [illegible] or not.
You further say that only by knowing those who transmitted the Way can one attain the highest achievement in approaching it. Possessing no such knowledge, how dare I hope to approach the Way? Yet I have spent years reciting and explaining the texts, and perhaps have privately discerned one or two things about the ancients. I have long thought that Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu, the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius are the ancestral authorities of the Way. Zhou was supremely refined, but his accomplishments were not yet extensive; Cheng was supremely correct, but his subtle teachings were not yet fully explicated. Xu was supremely pure, but perhaps did not fully explore the diversity of particular manifestations. Wu was supremely learned, but did not fully explore the unity of principle. As for one who brought refinement to its utmost and comprehensively penetrated what lies above [?], grasped the meaning of the unity of principle and the diversity of its manifestations, and possessed the excellence of abundant accomplishment and abundance [?], surely it was Zhu…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
子于固生之所願學者也若夫康節橫渠
南軒東萊則私淑程朱之奧惠龜山上蔡勉
齋西山皆非關洛之顏曾雖不敢望其藩
籬若所學則姑舍是執事以斯文相期不
敢不言其志惟進而教之
第三問
王酉星
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔薰鋼藩鎮新法乃中士子多能記述大畧至於治亂興衰古今時勢〕
===
逹識斷僅見此篇
同考試官教諭趙　批〔士子讀史乃經學之具此策出入漢唐宋諸史援引裁斷參以時事已見〕
如老將用兵部伍嚴肅料敵設機謀猷萬全子
蓋邃養靜觀而有得者
考試官教諭莫　批〔往事得失後人龜鑑士子平日看史無掩卷之思臨事鮮不復蹈舊轍吾〕
觀子所不滿於漢唐宋諸君子其所以自負待用
者可知矣允宜高薦
punctuated:
子，于固生之所願學者也。若夫康節、橫渠、南軒、東萊，則私淑程朱之奧惠；龜山、上蔡、勉齋、西山，皆非關洛之顏曾。雖不敢望其藩籬，若所學則姑舍是。執事以斯文相期，不敢不言其志，惟進而教之。
第三問
王酉星
同考試官教諭蔡批〔薰鋼、藩鎮、新法，乃中士子多能記述大畧。至於治亂興衰、古今時勢，〕逹識斷，僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭趙批〔士子讀史，乃經學之具。此策出入漢唐宋諸史，援引裁斷，參以時事，已見〕如老將用兵，部伍嚴肅，料敵設機，謀猷萬全。子蓋邃養靜觀而有得者。
考試官教諭莫批〔往事得失，後人龜鑑。士子平日看史，無掩卷之思，臨事鮮不復蹈舊轍。吾〕觀子所不滿於漢唐宋諸君子，其所以自負待用者可知矣。允宜高薦。
translation_en:
…Master Zhu is surely the one whom I have wished throughout my life to emulate [?]. As for Kangjie, Hengqu, Nanxuan, and Donglai, they privately imbibed the profound teachings and beneficence of Cheng and Zhu [?]; Guishan, Shangcai, Mianzhai, and Xishan are all not the Yan Hui and Zeng Shen of the Guan and Luo traditions [?]. Although I dare not hope even to approach their outer precincts, as for what I study, let us set this aside for now [?]. Since you place expectations upon me concerning this cultural tradition, I dare not leave my aspirations unstated. I ask only that you advance me and instruct me.
Third Policy Question
Wang Youxing
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “Xungang [?], the regional military commands, and the New Policies: candidates here [?] can mostly recount their broad outlines. But concerning order and disorder, rise and decline, and the circumstances of past and present, penetrating understanding and judgment are found only in this essay.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “Candidates’ reading of history provides resources for their study of the Classics. This policy essay ranges through the histories of the Han, Tang, and Song, adducing evidence and weighing judgments, and bringing contemporary affairs into the discussion. It already displays the qualities of a seasoned general commanding troops: the ranks are disciplined, the enemy is assessed and stratagems devised, and the plans are thoroughly sound. You must be someone who has attained understanding through profound self-cultivation and quiet contemplation.”
Comment by Examiner Mo, Instructor: “The successes and failures of past affairs provide guidance and a mirror for later generations. If candidates, in their everyday reading of history, never close the book to reflect, then when faced with affairs they seldom avoid repeating earlier mistakes. From what you find unsatisfactory in the gentlemen of the Han, Tang, and Song, one can discern the grounds of your confidence as you await employment. You certainly deserve a strong recommendation.”

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授宋　批〔古人議論行事得失能以意見縱横折辨曲盡治亂之原〕
天下之勢何能盡絶乎小人處之有道雖
小人不能爲君子之害天下之法何能盡
保其無弊救之以漸雖弊法不至爲天下
之禍夫天下既不幸有小人矣猶幸有君
子維持其間以救害之什一攻之太過而
授之以指摘之隙併其身與黨且不能一
日安乎其位而尚何能爲斯世斯民之□
===
乎法之不能無弊亦勢之不能免者勢不
能免而縱其弊之所至固必至於大壞極
亂而後已懼其大壞而竭力併智一舉而
更易之以快其意則其奔驟抗敵之勢將
不益助其弊以重爲天下之禍乎愚嘗謂
漢之黨錮君子之不善處乎小人也唐之
藩鎮不善救弊而聽其大壞者也宋之新
法既不能善處乎小人又不能救弊而急
之使變兩失之者也夫唐虞三代可謂治
punctuated:
考試官教授宋　批〔古人議論行事得失，能以意見縱横折辨，曲盡治亂之原。〕

天下之勢，何能盡絶乎小人？處之有道，雖小人不能爲君子之害。天下之法，何能盡保其無弊？救之以漸，雖弊法不至爲天下之禍。夫天下既不幸有小人矣，猶幸有君子維持其間，以救害之什一。攻之太過，而授之以指摘之隙，併其身與黨且不能一日安乎其位，而尚何能爲斯世斯民之□乎？法之不能無弊，亦勢之不能免者。勢不能免，而縱其弊之所至，固必至於大壞極亂而後已。懼其大壞，而竭力併智，一舉而更易之，以快其意，則其奔驟抗敵之勢，將不益助其弊，以重爲天下之禍乎？愚嘗謂，漢之黨錮，君子之不善處乎小人也；唐之藩鎮，不善救弊而聽其大壞者也；宋之新法，既不能善處乎小人，又不能救弊而急之使變，兩失之者也。夫唐虞三代，可謂治
translation_en:
Examiner Song, an Instructor, comments: 〔In discussing the merits and failings of the ancients’ arguments and actions, the author freely deploys his own judgments in analysis and refutation, thoroughly exploring the sources of order and disorder.〕

Given the circumstances of the world, how could petty men be eliminated altogether? If they are dealt with in the proper way, even petty men cannot harm gentlemen. How could the laws of the realm all be guaranteed free of defects? If these are remedied gradually, even defective laws need not bring calamity upon the realm. Although the world has the misfortune to contain petty men, it still has the good fortune to contain gentlemen who hold things together amid them and alleviate a tenth of the harm. If gentlemen attack them too fiercely and give them an opening for accusations, neither the gentlemen themselves nor their associates will be secure in their positions for even a day. How, then, could they still bring [illegible; ?] to this age and its people?

That laws cannot be free of defects is likewise an unavoidable consequence of circumstances. Yet if, because such defects are unavoidable, one allows them to run their course, they will assuredly culminate in utter collapse and extreme disorder. If, fearing that collapse, one exhausts one’s strength and musters all one’s ingenuity to change the laws at a single stroke, simply to satisfy one’s own wishes, will the resulting headlong rush and resistance not aggravate their defects and bring still greater calamity upon the realm?

I have often said that the Han prohibitions against partisan affiliations resulted from gentlemen’s failure to deal properly with petty men. The regional military commands of the Tang exemplified a failure to remedy abuses, allowing them to reach utter collapse. With the New Policies of the Song, there was both a failure to deal properly with petty men and a failure to remedy abuses; instead, precipitate action forced a crisis. This was failure on both counts. Now, the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and the Three Dynasties may be said to have attained order…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
之極矣然當時豈盡無小人弊法矣乎四
凶之比周管蔡之流言何異朋黨三苗之
負固羲和之黨羿何異藩鎮盤庚之起信
險膚太甲之顛覆典刑何異新法然禁之
則止誅之則滅更之則服豈非以其預防
而善處乎漢自陳蕃竇武用事而門戶已
立竇武劉淑爲君而標榜愈高夫小人之
類雖盛世不能盡無而君子之名在小人
未嘗不好別白太甚勢固激矣張儉□
===
鄉之微而舉劾中常王允以郡吏之賤□
捕殺黃門恥不與黨徒爲助火之薪□謝
霍諝過拘不實之諒其禍盡歸罪於小人
可乎唐自十道置使而藩鎮之根萌擴騎
募卒而藩鎮之權重十六宿衛之兵虛名空
伍邊塞之強兼統久任漁陽啓釁勢何能
已矣自後機會一失於肅宗而連州統郡

之極矣。然當時豈盡無小人弊法矣乎？四凶之比周、管蔡之流言，何異朋黨？三苗之負固、羲和之黨羿，何異藩鎮？盤庚之起信險膚、太甲之顛覆典刑，何異新法？然禁之則止，誅之則滅，更之則服，豈非以其預防而善處乎？漢自陳蕃、竇武用事，而門戶已立；竇武、劉淑爲君，而標榜愈高。夫小人之類，雖盛世不能盡無，而君子之名，在小人未嘗不好。別白太甚，勢固激矣。張儉□鄉之微，而舉劾中常；王允以郡吏之賤，□捕殺黃門。恥不與黨，徒爲助火之薪。□謝、霍諝過拘不實之諒，其禍盡歸罪於小人，可乎？
唐自十道置使，而藩鎮之根萌；擴騎募卒，而藩鎮之權重。十六宿衛之兵，虛名空伍；邊塞之強，兼統久任。漁陽啓釁，勢何能已矣？自後機會一失於肅宗，而連州統郡，無復節制之綱；姑息再縱於代宗，而易主更官，縱其驕橫之欲，甚至誘王弁而斬之
translation_en:
…the pinnacle of good government. Yet could those times have been entirely free of petty men and defective institutions? How did the collusion of the Four Evildoers and the rumors spread by Guan and Cai differ from factionalism? How did the Sanmiao’s reliance on their strongholds and Xi and He’s siding with Yi differ from the military governorships? How did the trusting of dangerous and superficial talk in Pan Geng’s time [?], and Tai Jia’s overthrow of established norms, differ from the New Policies? Yet when prohibited, these things stopped; when punished, they were extinguished; and when changes were made, people submitted. Was this not because precautions had been taken and matters were handled well?
Under the Han, once Chen Fan and Dou Wu took charge of affairs, factional divisions were already established; when Dou Wu and Liu Shu were acclaimed as “lords,” the mutual acclaim grew still more extravagant. Even in a flourishing age, petty men cannot be wholly absent; yet petty men themselves have never failed to cherish the reputation of a gentleman. When distinctions are drawn too sharply, the situation inevitably becomes inflamed. Zhang Jian, of humble standing in □ township [?], impeached a Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary; Wang Yun, despite his lowly position as a commandery clerk, □ arrested and killed a eunuch attendant [?]. Ashamed not to join the faction, men merely became fuel for the fire. □ Xie [?] and Huo Xu clung too rigidly to a misplaced conception of good faith. Can the blame for the resulting calamity be laid entirely upon petty men?
Under the Tang, the roots of the military governorships sprouted when commissioners were appointed to the ten circuits; as cavalry forces were expanded [?] and soldiers recruited, the power of those governorships increased. The troops of the sixteen palace guards existed in name only, their ranks empty; powerful commanders on the frontiers held combined commands and remained long in office. Once hostilities broke out at Yuyang, how could their momentum be checked? Thereafter, an opportunity was lost under Suzong: prefectures were joined together and commanderies placed under combined command, with no framework of regulation and restraint remaining. Under Daizong, indulgence again gave them free rein: they replaced their commanders and changed their officials, giving full scope to their arrogant and overbearing desires. Matters even reached the point of luring Wang Bian into a trap and beheading him…

title: 嘉靖十六年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
序曰自昔君子之大有建立
於天下也良不偶焉其初也
恒由養以充之其終也未嘗
不因於所遇以玉其成猶之
木然長養於山林之中雨露
之所膏潤煙霞之所披拂非
===
不森然秀穹然大也而柯幹
柔脆任重不力匠石者無取
焉逞之以歲時而卒遇霜雪
過之嚴凝寒凓之氣迭相摧
剝使其堅實挺直斯可登而
材也故一出而堪棟梁之用
以壯夫廟堂之觀吁亦難哉
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

序曰：自昔君子之大有建立於天下也，良不偶焉。其初也，恒由養以充之；其終也，未嘗不因於所遇以玉其成。猶之木然，長養於山林之中，雨露之所膏潤，煙霞之所披拂，非不森然秀、穹然大也，而柯幹柔脆，任重不力，匠石者無取焉。逞之以歲時，而卒遇霜雪過之，嚴凝寒凓之氣迭相摧剝，使其堅實挺直，斯可登而材也。故一出而堪棟梁之用，以壯夫廟堂之觀。吁，亦難哉！
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

The postface reads: From ancient times, the great accomplishments of gentlemen in the world have assuredly never come about by chance. At the outset, they invariably develop their capacities through cultivation; in the end, it is always through what they encounter that they are perfected, like jade. They resemble trees growing amid mountains and forests, nourished by rain and dew and brushed by mist and clouds. Such trees may indeed be luxuriant and lofty, yet if their branches and trunks are soft and brittle, unable to bear heavy loads, a master carpenter such as Shi will find no use for them. Give them the passage of years and seasons [?], however, and eventually frost and snow will sweep over them. As the forces of bitter, freezing cold batter and strip them in succession, they become firm and solid, straight and upright; only then can they be selected for timber. Thus, once brought forth, they can serve as ridgepoles and beams, lending grandeur to the halls of court. Ah, how difficult this is!
